AdvanceEventColumn:
Advance to the next column within an event block rectangle.

Decrements the column counter ($9E). If it reaches zero, returns carry set (SEC, row complete). Otherwise: advances pixel X ($1A) by 16, increments both source ($96) and destination ($9A) tile X coordinates, and moves both map indices right via MapIndexMoveRight. Returns carry clear (CLC, more columns remain).
AdvanceEventRow:
Advance to the next row of the event block rectangle.

Decrements the row counter ($A0); carry set (SEC) when all rows are done. Otherwise: pixel Y ($1E) += 16, source ($98) and destination ($9C) tile Y += 1, source X ($96) and destination X ($9A) are reloaded from the original event_block_table entry (offset kept in $A8, bytes +1 and +5), and the column counter ($9E) is reset from the width ($A2). Returns carry clear (more rows).
AnimateEventBlock:
Animated event block copy: same rectangle copy as CopyEventBlockTiles, but every copied tile inside the camera window also queues a 2×2 metatile VRAM update so the change appears progressively.

Layer 0 path (loc_02A3EF): copies mapLayerTilemap + collisionLayer, calls QueueVisibleTileVram with pixel positions $1A (X) / $1E (Y). Carry set (off-screen) advances to the next tile. Z set with carry clear (queue full) advances, writes the zero terminator at $0800+Y, calls UpdateFrameDialogue so the NMI flushes the queue, and restarts from the current tile with Y = 0.

Layer 1 path (code_02A443): copies effectLayerTilemap, resolves collision through [$3E] like CopyEventBlockTiles, and has its own inline visibility test (effectScrollH / effectScrollV) and queue code (metatileEffectLayer, VRAM address + $0800). When its queue fills and tiles remain it writes the terminator and returns carry clear: the caller must flush a frame and call again.

Returns carry set when every tile has been processed (terminator written), carry clear when interrupted by a full layer 1 queue. Uses DP = 0 and keeps all progress in $96-$A8, so a repeated call resumes where it stopped.
ApplyAllEventBlocks:
Apply every active event block for the current scene.

Walks the event flag bitfield at $0A20 in 8-bit chunks (LSR shifts each flag into carry). For each set flag the event index ($04) goes through LookupEventBlock; when the scene matches (carry clear), CopyEventBlockTiles copies the rectangle instantly. The outer loop ends when $04 wraps to zero (256 indices, 32 bytes).

Saves and restores processor state (PHP/PLP). The bitfield loop is 8-bit; the lookup call switches to 16-bit.
ApplyMovementDeltas:
Apply pending velocity to position and zero the velocity.

Adds $20 (X velocity) to $22 (X position) and $24 (Y velocity) to $26 (Y position), then zeroes both velocity words. Standard movement epilogue when the movement check determines no collision blocks the path.
ApplySlopeCurveNegEW:
Read the curve word at slopeCurvePtrA + (slopeStepCounter & $0F) x 2, negate it and add it to playerSpeedEw. A result of exactly zero jumps to SlopeSpeedZeroLatch (shared by all four curve routines: clear slopeStepCounter and set the $1000 latch); otherwise slopeStepCounter is incremented. Default curve: +1 every fourth step.
ApplySlopeCurvePosEW, ApplySlopeCurvePosNS and ApplySlopeCurveNegNS are the same routine for the positive EW curve, the positive NS curve (slopeCurvePtrB, playerSpeedNs) and the negated NS curve.
ApplySlopeCurveNegNS: Negated NS curve (slopeCurvePtrB): subtract the curve word from playerSpeedNs (northward). Speed zero -> SlopeSpeedZeroLatch; otherwise slopeStepCounter + 1.
ApplySlopeCurvePosEW: Positive EW curve (slopeCurvePtrA): add the curve word to playerSpeedEw (eastward). Speed zero -> SlopeSpeedZeroLatch (clear slopeStepCounter, set $1000); otherwise slopeStepCounter + 1. The label SlopeSpeedZeroLatch sits in this block but is also the target of the three sibling routines.
ApplySlopeCurvePosNS: Positive NS curve (slopeCurvePtrB): add the curve word to playerSpeedNs (southward). Speed zero -> SlopeSpeedZeroLatch; otherwise slopeStepCounter + 1.
ArrangeCancelTab: Cancel the Arrange tab. KillNext removes the cursor, the cancel bit ($4000) is consumed, and control returns to InventoryMainLoop.
ArrangeCancelTarget: Cancel target selection. COP KillNext kills second cursor, falls through to ArrangeCancelTab.
ArrangeItemsTab: Arrange tab action handler. Hides the equip cursor, spawns SelectionCursorActor (saved to $20), sets $22 = 0. Source loop: B ($4000) → ArrangeCancelTab, A ($8000) → ArrangePickTarget, D-pad → GridCursor* via the PEA/RTS trick (PEA pushes ArrangeSourceLoop − 1 as the return address of the GridCursor* RTS; when no button matched, PLA discards it).
ArrangePerformSwap: Execute the swap between source ($2E) and target ($22). Consumes the confirm bit; same-slot is ignored (back to the target loop). 8-bit swap of inventorySlots[$22] and [$2E] through XBA. Refreshes both slot actors: UpdateSlotActorSprite returns Y = the slot ACTOR, which is why STA $0028,Y after it addresses the actor. Equipped tracking: the first test (TYA; CMP inventoryEquippedIndex) compares that actor address, not a slot index, so "target slot was equipped" never matches (OQ-I028-2); the second test (source slot equipped → follow to $22) works. Kills the saved source cursor ($2C) via MarkDeath and returns to the source loop.
ArrangePickTarget: Second phase of Arrange: pick the swap target. Saves the source cursor ($20 → $2C, $22 → $2E), spawns a second SelectionCursorActor, draws the target strings. B ($4000) → ArrangeCancelTarget; mask $8044 → ArrangePerformSwap. The vanilla ROM tests only the confirm bit here; the transform widens it to $8044, which also accepts the X ($0004) and Y ($0040) bits of the default remap (OQ-I028-1).
ArrangeSourceLoop: First-phase Arrange poll: positions the grid cursor at slot $22, yields, B cancels the tab, A picks a source slot via ArrangePickTarget, or D-pad navigation returns through a pushed resume address.
ArrangeSourceReset: Arrange tab setup after spawning the selection cursor: clears blink counter $1C, draws Arrange tab BG3 strings, then enters ArrangeSourceLoop.
ArrangeTargetLoop: Second-phase Arrange poll after a source slot is saved in $2E/$2C: positions the target cursor, B cancels target pick, confirm mask $8044 runs ArrangePerformSwap, else grid navigation loops.
AttackInit:
Shared melee attack initialization for all four directions.

Keeps only the D-pad bits of joypadCurrent (AND #$0F00), then sets joypadHeld = D-pad | attack ($0080) so the attack button and the held directions read as consumed. Clears actor flag $0100. Plays character-form-specific SFX: Will = sound #01, Freedan/Shadow = sound #02.
AttackRedirect:
Mid-attack direction change — allows Will to redirect attacks.

Checks joypadCurrent for any D-pad direction ($0F00). If none is held it branches to AttackFinish. Otherwise it clears the attack bit ($0080) from joypadHeld (un-consuming the button) and falls into AttackFinish, which clears the D-pad bits of joypadHeld and returns to idle for a new dispatch.
AttackSouth:
South-facing melee attack for all character forms.

AttackInit keeps only the D-pad bits of joypadCurrent, sets joypadHeld = D-pad | attack and plays the form-specific SFX; AttackSouth then consumes the south D-pad bit ($0400) in joypadHeld. Freedan (form 1) checks for wall-adjacent attack via BranchIfSolidSouth — if wall contact, uses push sprite #48 instead of normal #36. Also checks diagonal solid offset for X-axis alignment.

Scene $00E8 (Dark Gaia fight): spawns ProjectileSouth alongside melee.

Per-frame loop: Will (form 0) checks every D-pad direction except south ($0B00 = Up|Left|Right) for a redirect and the facing direction ($0400) for the lunge. Freedan/Shadow check redirect only. On animation end, checks for attack button re-press (combo) or finishes.
AttackSystemEntry:
Attack dispatcher and Freedan ability implementations (178099–179702).

This part contains the attack companion actor's main dispatch logic plus all of Freedan's abilities. Despite being named after its first piece (AttackSystemEntry), the part spans the full attack dispatcher, both character-specific dispatch paths, all helper routines, and the complete Dark Friar and Aura Barrier ability implementations.

Major sections within this part:

1. Attack Dispatcher (178099–178432): AttackSystemEntry checks player state each frame and listens for the attack button (mask $0081, held level in joypadRaw). WillAttackDispatch handles Will's 40-frame hold + 120-frame charge with ability bitmask gating for Psycho Dash/Spin Dash. FreedanAttackDispatch handles Freedan's 40-frame hold + 100-frame charge with Dark Friar/Aura Barrier selection. LaunchPsychoDash, LaunchSpinDash, LaunchDarkFriar, and LaunchAuraBarrier validate and hijack the player actor function pointer.

2. Attack Helpers (178433–178558): AttackCleanup kills spawned FX and restores palette. SetPlayerActorFunc overwrites the player actor's entry point. ValidateAttackReady checks $3A00 flags and facing direction. ValidateAttackContinue does per-frame $2B00 checks. SavePlayerPosition snapshots position. CheckAttackChargeable returns carry clear only while playerFlags $8000 is clear and the player body animation index is 0-3 or $10-$13.

3. Aura Barrier (178559–178710): AuraBarrierMain sets flags, spawns VRAM DMA loader, waits for tile upload, loads FX palette, spawns orbital children, and runs the expand→orbit→shrink lifecycle. AuraBarrierEnd clears flags and returns to idle. AuraVramDmaLoader does a one-shot DMA of Aura tile graphics.

4. Aura Orbital System (178711–179002): AuraOrbitalSpawner spawns 2-4 orbital children (count depends on upgrade flag $0B1E), manages 240-frame orbit rotation expanding from diameter 0 to 64, then runs a 30-frame shrink. UpdateOrbitalPositions iterates children with angle spacing via ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef. AuraProjectileChild is the individual orbiting sprite with 3-frame animation. AuraProjectileShrink reverses the animation and flags for removal.

5. Dark Friar (179003–179701): DarkFriarMain sets flags, spawns VRAM DMA, loads palette, spawns a palette reset thinker (#4A), and dispatches by facing direction. Each directional handler (South/North/West/East) spawns a projectile and trail at character-appropriate offsets. DarkFriarProjectile is the initial flash sprite. DarkFriarTrailSouth and DarkFriarTrailEastWest are the growing trail actors with optional collision (enabled by upgrade level $0B1C). DarkFriarBounceLoop keeps the trail travelling until it leaves the screen, and at upgrade level 2 holding attack runs DarkFriarDisableCollide, which detonates it into fragments on demand. DarkFriarOnHit spawns 4 fragment actors at 90° intervals. DarkFriarFragmentInit sets up spiraling outward motion, DarkFriarFragmentLoop applies the reversed velocity every frame until the fragment leaves the screen (actor flag $4000), then it dies.
AutoAlignEW:
Auto-align player X position to the tile grid during vertical movement.

Called during north/south movement to prevent the player from catching on tile corners. Checks if the player's sub-tile X offset ($22 >> 2 − 8, AND $0F → $04) is in a nudgeable range:

Skip conditions (return SEC = no alignment):
  - $AA bit $0040 set (diagonal mode active — alignment handled elsewhere)
  - collisionLayer high nibble nonzero (special collision type)
  - Sub-tile offset is exactly 0 (already aligned)

Nudge toward lower grid (offset 6-8): Probes ProbeFutureTR — if collision is passable (< $0E, not $06), subtracts $20 from $22, calls NudgeToLowerGrid, restores +$20. Returns CLC (alignment applied).

Nudge toward upper grid (offset 1-8, via 9+ check): Probes ProbeFutureTL with the same passability check. Subtracts $20, calls NudgeToUpperGrid, restores +$20. Returns CLC.

The ±$20 offset adjusts the probe position to test the tile the player would enter after the nudge.
AutoAlignEW_South:
Corner assist for a blocked south step: nudge X by 2 pixels toward the open column. Returns carry CLEAR when X was nudged, carry SET when nothing happened.

Gates: $AA bit $0040 (the horizontal phase ran this tick), an actor solid mark in the collision byte at X, or n = 0 each return carry set. n = ((X >> 2) - 8) AND $0F is the left-edge offset inside its 16-pixel column (X is the centre, the left edge is X - 8). n >= 6: east nudge, if FutureBR is passable (< $0E): $22 is shifted by -$20 so the helper works on the left edge, NudgeToLowerGrid adds 8 sub-pixels, then +$20 restores the reference. n <= 8 (also when the east test failed): west nudge, if FutureBL is passable, through NudgeToUpperGrid (-8 sub-pixels). The old text had the ranges as '6-8' and '1-5'.
AutoAlignNS_East: Y auto-align before the east X snap. Carry set = no nudge: vertical velocity parked at $06,S nonzero, actor solid mark at the last probe cell, or n = (($26 >> 2) AND $0F) = 0. n >= 4: south nudge (NudgeToLowerGrid, $26 += 8) if FutureBR < $0E; else n <= 10: north nudge (NudgeToUpperGrid, $26 -= 8) if FutureTR < $0E. Carry clear = nudged. Structural mirror of AutoAlignEW (player_move_main) on the Y axis.
Bg3TilemapVramDma:
Uploads the BG3 tilemap staging buffer (bg3TilemapBuffer, WRAM $7F0200) to the BG3 tilemap in VRAM during V-Blank. BG3SC is initialised to $78, so VRAM $7800 is the BG3 tilemap (32×32 words = $0800 bytes), not sprite graphics; the buffer is the one the console string renderer writes. Called every NMI from system_core.

First checks hudDisableFlag ($09ED) bit 7 — if set, the upload is suppressed (returns immediately). Then checks displayModeFlags ($09EC) for bits $31 — if none are set, nothing is pending.

Two transfer modes based on flag bits:
1. Bit 0 (full update): Transfers $0800 bytes (the whole 32×32 BG3 tilemap) from WRAM $7F0200 to VRAM $7800.
2. Bits 4 or 5 (partial update): Transfers $0140 bytes (160 words = five tile rows) from WRAM $7F0280 to VRAM $7840 (tile row 2 onward). Bits 4 and 5 behave identically: the bit-5 path pre-clears that bit, but the common TRB below clears bits 0, 4 and 5 either way.

After the transfer, clears the request flags (bits 0,4,5 via TRB with $31). Sets VMAIN=$80, DMAP0=$01, BBAD0=$18, source bank=$7F, then triggers DMA channel 0. (displayModeFlags bit 3 is the separate player-tile DMA request handled in system_core.)
BitMaskTable: Single-bit mask lookup: $01,$02,$04,$08,$10,$20,$40,$80. Indexed by (item ID & 7).
BuildAttributeTable: Build a 256-byte metatile attribute lookup at $7E:2800. Zeroes $100 bytes at S_metatileEffectLayer, then walks $800 bytes of S_metatileMapLayer map-layer data in 2-byte steps: indexes by the low metatile byte, extracts the 3-bit palette field from the high byte (ASL×2, AND #$70), and stores into the attribute slot.
BuildMetatileFlagTable: Post-process a freshly loaded metatile definition table in WRAM bank $7E. X selects layer (0 or 2). Walks the tilemap words at $06AE+X (256 metatiles x 4 words; $0E starts at 0 so DEC wraps to 256 passes): for each word, lifts bit 9 out into a packed flag table and rewrites the word with bit 9 cleared (AND #$FDFF) and the layer merge word $06A2+X OR'd in (priority bit / tile offset from SceneCmd_ConfigDisplay). The four lifted bits of each group are combined via ASL/ORA/LSR into one byte stored through [$42] (pointer from $06AA+X, bank $7F), so the flag table holds one byte (low nibble = the four bit-9 flags, first tile in bit 0) per 2x2 metatile; FillCollisionFromLayer0/OverlayCollisionFromLayer1 later index it by metatile number to fill the collision layer.
CacheSlotIndices: ROM table of 4 three-byte entries (slot index 0, 1, 2, 3, then two zero bytes). Its only reader is scene_script.RestoreCachedVram, which takes the slot index, converts it to a WRAM source address $4000 + slot x $2000 (the 4-slot VRAM cache ring) and DMAs it back to VRAM; X selects the entry (3 bytes per entry).
CameraFullRefresh:
Full tilemap refresh — redraws the entire visible screen.

Wraps camera target positions into the map bounds with a bitmask (AND with bounds−1; an exact modulo only when the bound is a power of two). Copies the wrapped positions to the BG scroll registers ($068A+X for horizontal, $068E+X for vertical) and aligns to the 16px tile grid for rendering origin.

Sets up VRAM DMA registers: VMAIN=$81 (word-access, column-mode auto-increment), DMAP0=$01 (two-register), BBAD0=$18 (VRAM data port), source bank=$7E.

Iterates 32 metatile columns (32 × 16px = 512px, the full two-nametable width): for each column, calls RenderColumnStrip to build a 16-metatile vertical strip in the column staging buffer, then immediately DMA-transfers it via DmaColumnStrip. After each column, advances the X position ($18) by 16px and wraps it against the map width.

After all columns are rendered, clears the four staging buffer VRAM address words to prevent re-triggering, then calls UploadCgramPalette to sync the color palette.

Called during scene loading and major camera repositioning where the entire tilemap must be rebuilt.
CameraShakeFrame:
Per-frame camera shake offset calculation.

Two paths based on layerPriorityFlag bit 9 ($0200), the bit camera_scroll_controller treats as camera-frozen:
- Clear: zero the saved camera copies ($7F100C/E), then add random offsets to the camera targets using one RNG byte: (RNG & 3) - 1 to X, ((RNG >> 2) & 3) - 1 to Y. Each offset is -1, 0, +1 or +2.
- Set: save the original camera target in actor WRAM on the first call ($7F100C/E), restore it before applying the offsets each later call, so the shake stays centred on the frozen position.
CameraSmoothScroll:
Per-frame incremental smooth scrolling for both BG layers.

Three modes based on flags:
1. Direct mode (scrollModeFlags bit 3, i.e. $06EF bit 3): Copies camera targets directly to scroll registers without any smoothing, delta clamping or strip rendering.
2. Layer 1 delta mode (X≠0 and bit $0400 of the word at layerPriorityFlag/$06EE, i.e. $06EF bit 2): Copies cameraDeltaX/Y ($06C0/$06C4) straight into effectScrollH/V ($068C/$0690), so the second layer's scroll follows the camera delta instead of its own target. No strips are rendered.
3. Normal smooth scroll: For each axis (X then Y):
   a. Computes delta = target − current scroll position
   b. Clamps delta to ±16px maximum per frame for smooth motion
   c. Stores clamped delta (scrollDeltaXClamped/scrollDeltaYClamped)
   d. Applies delta to update the scroll position
   e. XORs old and new positions and tests bit 4 — if this bit changed, the camera crossed a 16px tile boundary
   f. On boundary crossing: calls UpdateScrollColumn (for X) or UpdateScrollRow (for Y) to render the newly-visible tile strip into the staging buffer

Because the delta is at most ±16px, bit 4 of the position changes at most once per frame, so at most one new column and one new row are rendered per layer per frame.
CancelVerticalPhase:
Cancel the vertical phase of the current movement tick.

Zeroes the 16-bit word at $05,S. With the JSR return address on top, that word is the vertical velocity PlayerMovementTick parked on its stack (PHA of $24), so the NS phase finds zero and does nothing. Called by the ramp handlers (here and in player_move_ramps), the ladder redirect and player_move_east.
CheckAttackChargeable:
Carry clear = the charge may continue and an L/R press may launch the alternate ability; carry set = not now.

Carry is set when playerFlags $8000 (body sprite override) is set, when the player actor animation index at +$28 is negative, or when it is neither 0–3 nor $10–$13. The Will dispatch only reads the L/R buttons while this routine returns carry clear.
CheckAttackWhileWalking:
Check for attack or speed-zero conditions during walking.

Called via JSR from WalkSouth/North/West/East per-frame loops. Checks:
1. Attack button (mask $0080) down → WalkAbortToIdle (pop return, restore saved ptr)
2. Both EW and NS speed zeroed (external stop) → WalkAbortToIdle
3. If neither: test playerFlags bit 12 ($1000, on-slope flag) and return the result in Z

Returns: Z = 0 means the on-slope flag is set, and every caller then branches over its L/R block check (BNE); Z = 1 (not on a slope) lets the caller test L/R for the block stance.
CheckInterleavedFlag: Alternate entry within SceneDmaTileShim. Tests layerPriorityFlag bit $0800 — if set, jumps to InterleaveTilesPriority for planar-to-priority tile conversion; if clear, falls through to DmaTileStripToVram for a normal WRAM→VRAM tile strip transfer.
CheckItemDiscardable: Test whether an item is non-discardable. A = item ID (not itemAbilityIndex): byte index = ID >> 3, bit = BitMaskTable[ID & 7], ANDed with the bit table at system_strings.non_discardable_item_bits. Carry set = protected (not discardable). Preserves X.
CheckRunAttack:
Psycho Slider eligibility gate — Will-only (form 0) running slide attack.

The Psycho Slider is Will's sliding attack ability (abilityBitmask bit 1, $0002), acquired in Mu West. When moving fast enough, pressing the attack button initiates a damaging slide that can pass through narrow passages.

Conditions (all must be true): actor flag $0080 clear (no hit-reaction counter active), characterForm == 0 (Will), abilityBitmask bit 1 ($0002) set (Psycho Slider learned), playerFlags bit 12 ($1000) clear (not on a slope). If all pass and the attack button (mask $0080) is down, branches to RunAttackSpeedCheck.
CheckSourceCacheHit: Compare current source pointer ($3E/$40) against cached entry at [$0000+X]. Address and bank match → return carry clear (cache hit, skip load). Mismatch → store new pointer to cache slot, return carry set (cache miss, load required).
CheckSubTileAlignX:
Test whether the X pixel coordinate ($1A) is aligned to a 16-pixel tile boundary.

Tests $1A AND $0F: if zero → carry clear (aligned), if nonzero → carry set (not aligned). Preserves A via PHA/PLA. Used after probes to determine whether the probe hit sits exactly on a tile edge.
CheckSubTileAlignY:
Test whether the Y pixel coordinate ($1E) is aligned to a 16-pixel tile boundary.

Tests $1E AND $0F: if zero → carry clear (aligned), if nonzero → carry set (not aligned). Preserves A via PHA/PLA. Mirrors CheckSubTileAlignX for the vertical axis.
CheckTileBoundaryXor:
Does the X step $20 move the player into a different 16-pixel column?

Computes (($22 >> 2) + ($20 >> 2)) XOR ($22 >> 2) (the XOR is with the PRE-step pixel, as the code comment says, not with the step) and tests bit 4 with BIT #$0010. The answer is in Z, not in carry: Z clear = a column boundary is crossed, Z set = no crossing; callers branch with BNE. The step is a logical shift, so a negative velocity becomes a large positive word, but it stays congruent to the signed step modulo $4000 and only bit 4 is used, so the result is still right.
CheckWarpAndChest:
Top-level entry point for warp detection and chest interaction.

Called once per frame from the main loop (system_core). Saves processor state, switches to 16-bit A, then calls CheckWarpRectangles first. Only if that reports no warp (carry clear) does it call HandleChestInteraction, so a warp takes priority over a chest. Both helpers return carry set on a hit, but the BCS after the chest call targets the very next instruction and PLP restores the caller's flags, so the routine returns no result; its effects are the staged warp parameters or the chest actions themselves. Four NOPs sit before the PLP (leftover padding, purpose unknown).
CheckWarpRectangles:
Test player position against all warp rectangles for the current scene.

Two passes — standard warps ($00D4, 12-byte entries) and extended warps ($00D6, 13-byte entries).

Each pass performs:
1. Tile-level AABB test: playerXTile minus entry X, compared against entry width; playerYTile minus entry Y, compared against entry height. Uses unsigned comparison (BCS = outside range).
2. Sub-tile pixel refinement: ConvertWarpToPixels converts tile coords to pixel bounding box. playerXPos/playerYPos minus origin, compared against extent.
3. On hit: standard warps → ExecuteWarp; extended warps → ExecuteForcedWalkWarp.

Entry stride: standard = $000C (12 bytes), extended = $000D (13 bytes). Both terminate on $FF sentinel byte.

If no warp hit: clears playerFlags bit $0100 (forced walk flag) and returns carry clear.
ChestDialogueActor:
Timed chest dialogue display actor.

One-shot actor spawned by ChestOpeningActor to show the item-get dialogue after a delay:
1. COP [WaitByte] ($48): waits 72 frames while the fanfare plays
2. Clears bit $1000 from its own actor flags ($12)
3. Copies the item ID it was given ($20) to $0DB8, where the string reads the item name
4. Calls ShowDialogueFrame with the dialogue string pointer stored in $24
5. COP [Die]
ChestOpeningActor:
Chest fanfare actor: item chests whose record has byte 3 bit 7 set are opened by this actor while the world is frozen (displayModeFlags bit 7), see the block note for the 6-step sequence.

Spawned by HandleChestInteraction with $26 = #$17 (track number), $24 = the dialogue string pointer from GiveItemToPlayer, $20 = the item ID, and flagged $1000. It spawns two SpcTransferMusicData children with SpawnAfterFlags: the first plays the track in $26 (+1) and the second restores the scene music saved from musicParentActor ($06F2) in orbitAngle. Registers are rotated with TXA/TYX/TAY so that X addresses the child while it is configured. Both spawns check for pool exhaustion (Y = $1FC0) and jump to code_02A88B. Yields use COP SetEntryHere with polling of musicTransitionState and APUIO1; the player is locked ($1000 flag, idle animation state, playerFlags $0800, joypad masked with $CFFC) until the SPC replies $FF.

code_02A88B: cleanup, clears displayModeFlags bit 7 and dies.
ClampSpeeds: Limit |speed| to maxSpeed - 1 (8 with the default maximum of 9). EW first: nonzero speed is compared (negated when negative) and clamped; the routine then returns without looking at NS. NS is only examined when the EW speed is zero. Called after every slope handler and from SlopeFlatExit.
ClearMovementDeltas:
Zero both movement velocity components ($24 = 0, $20 = 0).

Called when the player is fully blocked in a direction (e.g., sandwiched between two walls) to cancel all pending displacement. 16-bit mode (REP #$20) ensures both bytes are cleared.
ClearSpeedEW_5: Abort of the north-wall gap chain: playerSpeedEw = 0 and RTS. ApplyMovementDeltas is not run, so no position is applied this tick.
ClearSpeedEW_6: Abort of the south-wall gap chain: playerSpeedEw = 0 and RTS; no position is applied this tick.
ClearSpeedNS_1: Abort of the SouthWallHandler gap chain: playerSpeedNs = 0 and return. No position is applied this tick ($26 stays as it was).
ClearSpeedNS_2: Abort of the NorthWallHandler gap chain: playerSpeedNs = 0 and return. No position is applied this tick.
ClearSpeedNS_3: Zero playerSpeedNs and return; no position change. Used by the $09 gap test when a neighbouring cell is occupied.
ClearSpeedNS_4: Zero playerSpeedNs and return; no position change. Used by the $06 gap test (SouthWallSouthInteract and SouthSlideJumpShim).
ClearVramBufferFull: Clear the entire BG3 staging buffer ($7F:0200) from offset $0000 to $0800 (2048 bytes) by writing zero words in a loop. A following flush (displayModeFlags bit 0) uploads the cleared words to BG3.
ClearVramBufferPartial: Clear the BG3 staging buffer from offset $0140 to $0800. Keeps the first 320 bytes (the HUD rows written by LoadHudTilemap). Shares the write loop with ClearVramBufferFull.
ClimbDropAttack:
Freedan drop attack from vine — triggers ground impact effects.

Pops the climb loop return address, sets body sprite #06 with hitbox #00. Falls with force Y movement until hitting solid ground (16-pixel boundary check). On landing, loads anim table B entry 2, spawns ImpactTerrainShake and CameraShakeActor (scene $DD skips terrain shake), then plays 39-frame recovery animation before returning to idle.
ClimbVineEntry:
Vine climbing state machine — Freedan-only traversal system.

Entry: clear actor flag $0008 (restored by ClimbVineLand), set actor flag $0200, hide the use-item button ($0008) via joypadMaskStd. Plays initial climb-on animation (sprites #18, #19).

Main loop: 3-sprite alternating cycle (#1A, #1B, #19) with force Y movement (#07 = downward). Each frame checks for solid ground landing. CheckClimbFrame reads the $2A event flag for animation timing. CheckClimbAttack gates drop attack to Freedan (characterForm == 1) with abilityBitmask bit 6 ($0040).
code_028CB0: Continuation of SceneCmd_LoadCharTiles VRAM targeting (reached via PEA+RTS from bit-0 path). Tests flag bit 1 for VRAM $1800, else restores flags and returns without DMA; shared loc_028CC4 performs HDMA-style VRAM upload setup.
code_02EE17: Main loop of the inventory scene: one UpdateFrameDialogue per pass, then bg1ConfigMode is copied to BG1SC (the inventory_menu actor changes it to flip between the item grid and the status view). Exits when flag byte #00 becomes nonzero; eventFlags was zeroed at open, so the loop starts armed.
CombinedProbe_Unused:
Unreferenced combined tile probe — checks collision at a computed position with optional adjacent-cell fallback.

Entry: A = Y velocity component (caller-supplied), $22/$20 = X sub-pixel position/velocity, $26 = Y sub-pixel position, $1A = X pixel offset (added to computed X pixel).

Converts (A + $26) >> 2 → Y pixel, ($22 + $20) >> 2 + $1A → X pixel, probes TileProbeMain. If collision type ≥ $0E (blocking), returns carry set. If not blocking but Y pixel is not 16px-aligned, also probes MapCellUp for adjacent collision. Returns carry set if either probe ≥ $0E.

Marked _Unused: no call sites found in the codebase. Likely a debug or cut routine.
ComputeAbilityIndex: Compute the global ability index characterForm × 4 + abilitySlot + 1 and store it in itemAbilityIndex ($0AE8), the index the BG3 ability description strings use. Preserves A. (The meaning of "+1" is inferred from the earlier note; entry 0 of the description table was not checked.)
ComputeEastSnapOffset: Builds the push offset $02 for the east wall slide: ($1A AND $0F), plus $10 on the wall path when the step carries the probe across a 16-px column line. Wall path: current TR $09, or Y straddling with $06 in the cell below the current TR. The saved probe pixels $1A / $1E are restored before the final sum.
ComputeParentOffset:
Will ability implementations, projectile actors, palette FX, and utility routines (179826–181132).

This part contains all of Will's ability code plus shared helper routines. Despite being named after its first piece (ComputeParentOffset), the part spans offset helpers, the complete Psycho Dash and Spin Dash implementations, the guided projectile actor, all palette FX actors, and animation table loaders.

Major sections within this part:

1. Offset Helpers (179826–179871): ComputeParentOffset stores the XY delta between current position and a parent actor. ApplyParentOffset adds the stored delta back to the parent's current position. Used by Dark Friar projectile/trail actors to maintain relative positioning.

2. Psycho Dash (179872–180392): PsychoDashMain loads animation table A entry 0, disables status display, dispatches by facing. Each directional handler (South/North/West/East) spawns a trail afterimage actor, sets the movement direction via force flags, stages movement index $36 (a delta chain, not a distance), then returns to idle. The four PsychoDashTrail actors (South/North/West/East) record 8 position deltas during the dash and replay them in reverse as afterimage segments.

3. Spin Dash (180393–180763): SpinDashMain sets $2002 flags, enters a charge loop that aborts when the actor is hit (flag bit 7, $0080), then transitions to either the charge tick phase (L/R shoulder decrement charge level) or projectile launch. On launch, spawns GuidedProjectileActor, kills it on completion, and uses an RTS-trick (PEA label-1) to chain through directional speed setup → SpinDashRelease → SpinDashLaunch. SpinDashChargeTick alternates the L/R test by the parity of the charge level. SpinDashAbort clears flags and restores state.

4. Guided Projectile (180764–180999): KillSpawnedProjectile cleans up a stored actor reference via MarkDeath. GuidedProjectileActor stores its offset from the player, responds to D-pad input for 4-directional steering (Right=#3D, Left=#3C, Up=#3B, Down=#3A sprites), and runs a per-frame animation/collision loop.

5. Palette FX & Utilities (181000–181131): WillAttackPaletteFX cycles palettes #2A→#2B. FreedanAttackPaletteFX cycles #4B→#2C. AuraBarrierPaletteFX loops #5B infinitely. RecomputeProjectilePos adds stored offsets to current player position. LoadAbilityAnimTableA reads will_ability_anim_table (Will), LoadAbilityAnimTableB freedan_ability_anim_table (Freedan). Both store the damage byte for the current upgrade level to climbStateData ($09E0 Will, $09E2 Freedan); see the block note.
ComputeRingBufferAddr: Compute WRAM ring-buffer slot address from current index $0094. DEC, ROR×4 to place the 2-bit index into bits 13–14, AND #$6000, ADC #$4000. Yields $4000, $6000, $8000, or $A000 (each slot holds $2000 bytes).
ComputeSlotPosition: Look up slot screen position. inventoryTabIndex − 1 (0-based) × 4 indexes SlotPositionTable. Writes to $14/$16.
ComputeSouthSnapOffset: Computes $02, the penetration measure for the wall slide: low nibble of the probe Y ($1E AND $0F) plus $10 when the south step crosses a 16-pixel row line. The wall path (current BL is $09, or the cell right of a straddling hitbox is $06) tests the crossing: with v = $24 >> 2 and Y the restored probe Y, bit 4 of ((Y - v) XOR Y) set means the row line was crossed. All other cases use the low nibble alone. $1A / $1E are saved on the stack and restored before the final add, so the caller's probe coordinates survive.
ComputeWallSlidePush:
Compute the push distance used by WallSlidePushUp / WallSlidePushDown, left in $02.

Saves $1A/$1E. If the current TL tile is $09, or the Y row is off the 16-pixel boundary (CheckSubTileAlignY carry set) and the cell below is $06, the probe X is restored and the X velocity (converted to pixels) is subtracted from it; when that moves it into a different 16-pixel column (bit $0010 of the XOR) $10 is added to $02. Final $02 = (16 - ($1A & $0F)) + the accumulated adjustment, so the push depends on how far the player is across the tile in X.
ComputeYSnapOffset:
Compute a Y-axis snap correction to align the player to the next tile boundary.

Reads the low nibble of $1E (sub-tile Y position within the 16px grid), inverts it via two's complement: OR $FFF0 (sign-extend to 16-bit), XOR $FFFF + INC (negate). The result in $02 is the number of sub-pixels to add to snap Y downward to the tile boundary.

For example: if $1E low nibble = $04, the offset is $000C (12 pixels to the next boundary). If $00, offset is $0000 (already aligned).
ConvertWarpToPixels:
Convert warp rectangle tile coordinates to pixel bounding box.

Reads 4 bytes from the warp entry at X:
  Byte 0 → $00: origin X (tile × 16 = pixel)
  Byte 1 → $02: origin Y (tile × 16)
  Byte 2 → $04: width (tile × 16 − 15 = pixel extent)
  Byte 3 → $06: height (tile × 16 − 15)

The caller tests (player pixel − origin) < extent with an unsigned compare, so the player's pixel position must lie in [origin, origin + 16×size − 16]: the last 15 pixels of the rectangle (and anything left of or above it) do not trigger. This adds a pixel check on top of the tile check.
CopyEventBlockTiles:
Copy a rectangle of tiles from the source position over the destination position (the source is not modified, so this is a copy, not a swap).

Entry: parameters at WRAM $0096-$00A4 as loaded by LookupEventBlock, read through DP with D = 0: $96/$98 source X/Y tile, $9A/$9C destination X/Y tile, $9E columns remaining, $A0 rows remaining, $A2 original width, $A4 layer flag (0 = layer 0, nonzero = layer 1).

Layer 0 path (loc_02A264): per tile, copies mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer bytes from the source map index ($02) to the destination index ($00); MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown traverse the rectangle.

Layer 1 path (loc_02A2B9): same traversal on effectLayerTilemap. The collision byte comes from an indirect lookup: $3E/$40 hold the collision flag table pointer ($06AC, bank $7F) and the tile ID replaces the low byte of $3E, so [$3E] returns the table entry for that tile. The collision byte is written only if the entry is non-zero (empty overlay tiles keep the existing collision).
CountTitleGlyphs:
Count visible character width of a scene title wide-string.

Walks the byte stream at [$3E] + 1 (INC $3E skips a leading type byte). Accumulates glyph count in $00. Handles the command subset used in scene title strings:

- Bytes < $C0: literal tile characters — increments count by 1
- $CA (Return): end of string — returns with count in $00
- $CC (AdvanceCursor): reads 1-byte operand as additional glyph width, adds to count
- $D6 (DictionaryA): resolves compressed word from dictionary_01EBA8. Reads 1-byte index, looks up the word pointer (index × 2 + base), then counts each character until $CA terminator
- $D7 (DictionaryB): same as $D6 but uses dictionary_01F54D
- Other commands (≥ $C0): skips one operand byte without counting

The dictionary expansion switches DBR to the dictionary bank (PHA/PLB), saves/restores Y across the lookup, and returns to the main loop after counting all expanded characters.
DarkFriarDisableCollide: Reached from the bounce loop when the Dark Friar upgrade level is 2 and the attack button is held (joypadRaw). It clears the collide callback and then FALLS THROUGH into DarkFriarOnHit (there is no branch or return between the two blocks), so at level 2 holding attack detonates the trail into the four fragments on demand, with the callback removed so it cannot fire twice.
DarkFriarTrailNorthInit: Spawn entry stub for the north Dark Friar trail: sets bit $2000 in actor $12 to negate Y movement so the shared south trail code runs upward, then falls into DarkFriarTrailSouth.
DecelerateEW: EW flat-ground deceleration (details in the block note). Return at once while the $1000 latch is set. |speed| < 3 -> speed = 0 (decelStepCounter not reset). Positive speed: D-pad right ($0100) held -> return; otherwise one ReadDecelerationStep value is subtracted (speed 0 -> reset decelStepCounter, return), then, also when that value was 0, D-pad left ($0200) held applies a second step. Negative speed mirrors this with left suppressing and right braking. Each ReadDecelerationStep call advances decelStepCounter, so braking uses the curve twice per frame.
DecelerateNS: NS counterpart of DecelerateEW: same latch test, |speed| < 3 snap, same-direction suppression (down $0400 for positive speed, up $0800 for negative), one step plus a braking step for the opposite D-pad direction. Difference: when the speed reaches zero it clears slopeStepCounter (loc_02B76C) where DecelerateEW clears decelStepCounter, so after an NS stop the deceleration curve keeps its position.
DecelResetCounterEW: Tail inside DecelerateEW when east-west speed reaches zero after a decel step: clears decelStepCounter and returns with RTS; also used from the west-moving decel paths.
DeinterleavePlanarTiles: Initialize priority-deinterleave path: invalidates source-cache slots $066F, $067E, $0681, $0678 and $067B (zeroing addr-hi + bank at $0670/$067F/$0682/$0679/$067C), presumably because the interleaved $4000-byte upload to VRAM $0000 replaces what they describe, then decompresses tile data via QuintetLZ to $7000. Falls through into InterleaveTilesPriority for the actual bitplane interleaving pass.
DiagRedirectToNorth:
Fallback of WestRampAscend when no $0A tile was found.

ProbeFutureBL: type $09 enters DiagWallNorthFromDL, which falls into the code_02DC9F wall handler. Anything else applies the movement unchanged.
DiagRedirectToSouth:
Fallback of WestRampDescend when no $05 tile was found.

ProbeFutureTL: type $06 enters DiagWallSouthFromDL, which falls into the code_02DC4B wall handler. Anything else applies the movement unchanged.
DiagSnapCompute_Unused:
Unused diagonal movement snap computation with slope tile detection.

Saves pixel positions $1A/$1E, probes the current tile via ProbeCurrentTL. If the tile is type $06 (transition), or sub-tile X alignment + adjacent $09 check passes, computes a combined snap offset incorporating a $10 (16-pixel) slope correction in $02.

The main snap calculation takes the NS velocity ($24), converts to pixel offset (>>2, OR $C000 for sign preservation), negates, adds to $1E, and XORs with the original to detect a 16px boundary crossing (BIT #$0010). If crossed, $02 gets $0010 added.

Finally adds the standard Y snap offset (same as ComputeYSnapOffset) to $02.

Not called by any active code — appears to be a development-era diagonal collision experiment that was superseded by the current DispatchDiag* system.
DisableNmiKeepJoypad:
Write $01 to NMITIMEN ($4200): joypad auto-read ON, NMI OFF.

Bit 7 clear disables the NMI; bit 0 keeps the joypad auto-read enabled. The routine is called after the main loop's VBlank sync so that the frame's logic runs without NMI interruption, and by the SPC transfer routines around the port handshakes. EnableNmiAndJoypad turns the NMI back on.
DiscardAttempt: Discard attempt (label is an auto name). Consumes the confirm bit. Empty slot or protected item (CheckItemDiscardable carry set) → SFX #12 and back to the grid. Otherwise draws the item name and the "Discard? No / Yes" prompt ($28 = 0 = No) and polls YesNoPromptLoop once per frame (RTL while carry is clear). Answer No ($28 = 0) → back to the grid. Answer Yes: clears the slot's item byte (16-bit AND #$FF00 keeps the next slot's byte), refreshes the slot actor, clears inventoryEquippedIndex/Type and $1A if that slot was equipped, SFX #13.
DiscardCancelTab: Cancel the Discard tab. Consumes the cancel bit ($4000), kills the cursor, shows the equip cursor again, returns to InventoryMainLoop.
DiscardGridLoop: Discard tab poll: positions cursor, B leaves the tab, A runs DiscardAttempt, D-pad moves the grid with resume on the stack.
DiscardGridReset: Discard tab setup: clears $1C, draws Discard tab BG3 strings, then enters DiscardGridLoop.
DiscardItemTab: Discard tab handler. Sets bg1ConfigMode = 4, hides the equip cursor, spawns SelectionCursorActor, $22 = 0. Grid loop: B ($4000) → DiscardCancelTab, A ($8000) → DiscardAttempt (discard attempt), D-pad → GridCursor*.
DispatchEastMove: Entry for positive $20, 8-bit probe mode. Order, exits and the blocked path are described in the block note: JMPs into player_move_ramps or the wall handlers, the plain step $22 += $20, or the blocked path loc_02D753.
DispatchNorthMove: Entry for negative $24, 8-bit probe mode, called from PlayerMovementTick after the horizontal phase. Probe order, the plain step and the blocked path are described in the block note; exits are JMPs into the slope / wall handlers, the plain step (loc_02D0A5) or the blocked path (loc_02D0AF).
DispatchSouthMove:
Main entry for positive $24. Reads the left foot's current type first ($09, $03, $0C), then the right foot's ($06), then the destination under the left foot (FutureBL), and finally the second column when the hitbox straddles two columns. The non-blocked path ends with $26 += $24 only.

Register state: the routine runs with A 8-bit for the type compares and X/Y 16-bit; after ProbeFutureBL, X and $00 hold FutureBL's map index, which MapCellRight steps from.
DispatchWestMove:
Entry of the west (negative $20) horizontal-phase dispatcher; called once per tick by PlayerMovementTick.

Sets $AB bit 1 (SouthWallNudge in player_move_ns reads it as 'the west dispatcher ran this tick'), then probes in this order:
1. map_coords.FindSlopeForWestMove: slope search at the hitbox's centre column. Z clear = no slope; Z set with carry set = type $05 (WestRampDescend), carry clear = type $0A (WestRampAscend).
2. ProbeCurrentTL: type $06 goes to code_02DC4B. ProbeCurrentBL: type $09 goes to code_02DC9F.
3. ProbeFutureTL: $0E and above is a wall collision, $06 goes to code_02DC77 (the variant entry of the same handler).
4. CheckSubTileAlignY (carry clear = Y on a 16-pixel boundary): aligned, future-TL type $09 goes to code_02DCCB. Off the boundary: $09 is a wall collision, then the cell below (MapCellDown) is read: $0E and above blocks, $09 goes to code_02DCCB, $06 blocks.
5. Type $07 goes to DiagLadderTile. ProbeCurrentTR: $05 goes to WestRampEdgeDescend, $0A to WestRampEdgeAscend.
6. Otherwise $22 += $20.

Wall collision path: SetActorCollisionFlag, AutoAlignYToGrid, SnapXWestCollision.
DisplaySceneTitle:
Display the current scene's area name in a centered dialogue box overlay.

Called from ClearSceneState after actor spawning. Compares $0D6E (scene just left) with sceneCurrent and returns when they are equal.

Pipeline:
1. CountTitleGlyphs measures the title string at [$3E]
2. Returns if the count is zero (no title for this scene)
3. Centering offset: (18 − count) forced even, pushed for later
4. $00B4 = $E0 (wait-for-button flag for ExecuteSceneTransition), $00B5 = 0
5. Saves $40 and the title pointer $3E (in Y), sets DBR to this bank
6. DialogStringRenderer with scene_title_box_format opens the box
7. Restores the pointer, adds the offset to the VRAM cursor ($0998)
8. DialogStringRenderer again renders the title, then restores DBR and flags
DmaColumnStrip:
Transfers one COLUMN strip (a 16px-wide metatile column = two adjacent tile columns) from the staging buffer to VRAM via DMA. This is the strip used for horizontal scrolling: the caller sets VMAIN=$81, so each word lands 32 words (one tile row) after the previous one.

The staging buffer layout for each strip: [VRAM_addr:u16, data:64_bytes, VRAM_addr:u16, data:64_bytes]. The two halves are the left and right tile columns of the metatile column (VRAM address and address+1) — not two nametables.

First DMA: Sets VMADDL to the first VRAM address (from Y parameter), sets A1T0L to the staging data pointer (X+2), transfers $40 bytes (64 bytes = 32 tilemap entries = one full 32-tile-high column).

Second DMA: Advances the source pointer by $40 bytes, reads the second column's VRAM address, and transfers another $40 bytes.
DmaFixedByteFill: Fills Y bytes of WRAM, starting at the current WMADD address, with a zero byte read from ROM. DMA channel 0 mode $08 (fixed source address, one register), B-bus $80 (WRAM data port), source = first byte of math_lookup_tables.sine_table_8bit (sin 0 = $00). The WRAM address advances across banks, so the caller does not have to reset it between passes.
DmaLowVramTileset: DMA tile data directly to low VRAM ($2000, $4000 bytes). Reads compressed pointer from [$3E]; if non-null, decompresses to $7E:A000 and DMAs from there; if null, DMAs from the raw ROM pointer. Uses VMAIN=$00 (sequential byte), mode $00, B-bus $18; restores VMAIN=$80 after transfer.
DmaRomToWram: DMA or copy from ROM to WRAM with SNES address-space handling. HiROM path (source bank ≥ $80 with addr ≥ $8000, or bank ≥ $C0): hardware DMA — source = $3E+$0664, dest = $42+$0668 → WMADDL, size = $0666−$0664, WMADDH=1 when dest bank is $7F. LoROM path (bank < $80): software copy via JSR $0402 with banks at $0404/$0405 and byte count = ($0666−$0664)−1.
DmaRowStrip:
Transfers one ROW strip (a 16px-tall metatile row = two adjacent tile rows) from the staging buffer to VRAM via DMA. This is the strip used for vertical scrolling.

Same buffer layout as DmaColumnStrip but each half is $80 bytes (128 bytes = 64 words): with VRAM increment 1 the first 32 words fill one tile row of a nametable and the next 32 words fill the tile row below it. The two halves are the two nametables (the 512px strip is split across them); the second half's header is at source+$80.

VMAIN must be set to $80 (word-access, increment by 1) by the caller, unlike column strips, which need increment 32.
DmaTileStripToVram: DMA a tile data strip from WRAM ($3E+$0664, bank $40) to VRAM. Sets VMADDL from $0668 (XBA for page alignment), transfer size = $0666 − $0664. Configures channel 0: mode $01 (two-register word write), B-bus $18 (VMDATAL), triggers MDMAEN.
DmaVramToRam: DMA from VRAM to WRAM (reverse direction). Sets transfer size from A, calls ComputeRingBufferAddr for destination, primes read via VMDATALREAD. DMA mode $81, B-bus $39 (VMDATAHREAD), source bank $7F; restores DMAP0 to $01 afterward.
DmaWordToVram:
DMA channel 0 word transfer to VRAM.

Input: X = source address (16-bit), A = source bank byte, Y = transfer byte count.
Configures: DMAP0 = $01 (word transfer mode, 2-register write to $2118/$2119), BBAD0 = $18 (VDATA port).
Fires DMA via MDMAEN bit 0.
Caller must pre-set VMADDL ($2116) to the target VRAM word address, and VMAIN ($2115) must already be configured (this routine does not touch it).
Register width on entry: A 8-bit (bank byte, `LDA #$01` immediates), X/Y 16-bit. Callers: LoadPlayerGraphics (scene_lifecycle) and the inventory overlay.
DmaWramToVram: DMA from WRAM to VRAM. Sets VMADDL from $0668 (XBA), source address X, size Y. Mode $01, B-bus $18 (VMDATAL), source bank $7F. Returns in 16-bit mode (REP #$20).
DrawChestTiles:
Draw 2×2 chest tiles on the map and queue VRAM updates.

Entry: X = chest record pointer (scene_chest_table), $06 = base tile ID ($FC open, $F8 closed).

Reads the record's X/Y tile (bytes 0-1; Y is the bottom row, so the top row is Y−1) and keeps the pixel position of the top-left cell (×16) in $1A/$1E for QueueVisibleTileVram, which only queues the tile if that position is on screen. The map index comes from TileCoordsToMapIndex.

Writes four tiles in order, calling QueueVisibleTileVram after each:
  Top-left: base+2, Top-right: base+3
  Bottom-left: base, Bottom-right: base+1

The pixel coordinates in $1A/$1E follow the cell being drawn (+16 for each step right or down); MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown step the map index. At the end it terminates the VRAM queue with a zero word (written at dmaSkipFlag,Y) and calls UpdateFrameRender to flush the display immediately.
EastLadderTile: Type $07 ahead while moving east (a local label inside DispatchEastMove). CheckSubTileAlignY: Y straddling (carry set) -> blocked path. Y flush: CancelVerticalPhase cancels the vertical phase, the player actor's entry becomes ShimmyRightEntry (low word only) with $0008 = 0, then the blocked path runs (collision flag, Y nudge, X snap). Mirror of DiagLadderTile (ShimmyLeftEntry) in player_move_west. The old 'West prefix' remark refers to a former name; ShimmyRightEntry is the east case.
EastRampDown: Entered when FindSlopeForEastMove found $0A: descend while moving east. Samples: TR probe at (X, top row); the cell below it; FutureTR at (X + step - 1); the cell below that. Hits on the first two take the direct step (code_02D8C7); hits on the last two take the column-crossing test; no hit -> EastRedirectToNorth. See the block note.
EastRampUp: Entered from DispatchEastMove when ProbeCurrentBL read $0A. Samples (X, bottom + 1); not $0A -> ApplyMovementDeltas. $0A with no column crossing -> the direct step (Y += $20); with a crossing $24 = $20 - 4n (n = pixels past the column line after the step). Finishes at code_02D8CE.
EastRedirectToNorth:
Fallback when no slope tile is found after the full EastRampDown probe sequence.

Probes FutureTR: if $09 (north wall) → redirect to EastWallNorthDiag for diagonal wall interaction. Otherwise → ApplyMovementDeltas (continue movement unimpeded).
EastWallNorthDiag: A single SEP #$20 that falls into EastWallPushDown. player_move_ramps jumps here when its post-ramp FutureTR probe reads $09.
EastWallNorthFlag: Compact entry used when the future TR is already known to be $09: sets $AB bit 2 (no reader) and joins the gap chain at loc_02D7AB, skipping the probe and the X alignment test. ClearSpeedEW_5 is the shared abort: playerSpeedEw = 0 and return.
EastWallPushDown: Wall-slide handler for TR $09 while moving east. Sets $AB bit 7, ProbeFutureTR, CheckSubTileAlignX. X straddling and $09: gap chain (loc_02D7AB). Otherwise SnapYNorthCollision (player goes DOWN to the next row line), re-probe: clear or $09 -> slide, else SnapXEastCollision + ApplyMovementDeltas. Slide: ComputeEastSnapOffset + WallSlidePushDown, which pushes Y DOWN (positive $24); the old text said up (OQ-I029-4). See the block note.
EastWallPushUp: Wall-slide handler for BR $06 while moving east. Sets $AB bit 7, ProbeFutureBR, CheckSubTileAlignX. X straddling and $06: gap chain (loc_02D7FF): MapCellUp (empty or $05), then MapCellLeft (empty or $06). Otherwise SnapYSouthCollision (Y floored, up to 15 px north), re-probe: clear or $06 -> slide, else SnapXEastCollision + ApplyMovementDeltas. Slide: ComputeEastSnapOffset + WallSlidePushUp, which pushes Y UP (negative $24); the old text said down.
EastWallSouthDiag: A single SEP #$20 that falls into EastWallPushUp. player_move_ramps jumps here when its post-ramp FutureBR probe reads $06.
EastWallSouthFlag: Entry for a future TR / BR $06 (from DispatchEastMove): STX $00 (X still holds the map index of the last probe or MapCell step), sets $AB bit 3 (no reader) and joins the gap chain at loc_02D7FF. ClearSpeedEW_6 is the shared abort.
EnableNmiAndJoypad:
Enable NMI and joypad auto-read by writing $81 to NMITIMEN ($4200).

Bit 7 = enable NMI on V-Blank.
Bit 0 = enable joypad auto-read (hardware reads controller data during V-Blank into $4218–$421F).

Reads RDNMI first to clear any pending NMI flag, preventing an immediate spurious interrupt.
EnterForcedBlank:
Set INIDISP ($2100) to $80 — enter forced blank for VRAM access.

Sets bit 7 (forced blank on) with brightness 0. The PPU stops rendering, making VRAM, OAM, and CGRAM freely accessible for DMA transfers. Called before bulk VRAM operations.
EquipCursorActor: Equip cursor init. If inventoryEquippedIndex ≥ 0 → falls through to SelectionCursorActor. If negative ($FFFF) → set $2000 (hide) and fall through.
EquippedItemDisplay: Static equipped item icon at ($0028, $0078). Loads inventoryEquippedType as sprite, renders one frame.
ExecuteForcedWalkWarp:
Handle extended (forced-walk) warp — in-scene camera pan with player automation.

Entry: X = pointer to the 13-byte extended warp entry. Guard: if playerFlags bit $0100 (forced walk already active) is set it returns immediately (RTS) to prevent re-triggering.

Setup (the fields are shared with ExecuteWarp but hold different data here):
  warpFacing ($0650): a 16-bit POINTER to entry+7, the stream of 6 walk-step bytes that the ForcedWalk actors advance one byte per step (ReadDirSprite_*Velocity); not a facing byte
  playerSpeedEw/playerSpeedNs: zeroed (player movement stops)
  warpScrollParams ($0652): entry bytes 4-5, packed camera window read by InitCameraBounds (0 = normal bounds)
  scrollStepTableBase: entry byte 6 (low nibble = walk sequence index into forced_walk_sequence_table, bits 4/5/7 = direction)

Calls InitCameraBounds to configure camera limits for the destination area, then StartForcedWalk to spawn the appropriate directional walk actor. Returns carry set.
ExecuteWarp:
Execute a standard scene-transition warp.

Entry: X = pointer to the 12-byte standard warp entry. Copies it into the transition parameters:
  $0AF4/$0AF6: pointer to entry+4 and the scene_warps bank (GameOverSequence revive point, 100+ gems)
  sceneNext ($0642): Destination scene ID (entry byte 4)
  warpDestX/warpDestY ($064C/$064E): Destination X/Y words (entry bytes 5-6, 7-8)
  warpFacing ($0650): Facing/flags (entry byte 9)
  warpScrollParams ($0652): Scroll parameters (entry bytes 10-11)
  sourceSceneId ($0B12): sceneCurrent
  $0B08/$0B0C/$0B0A/$0B0E: Source warp rectangle (entry bytes 0-3)

Camera bytes: $0B10 = bits 8–11 of cameraOffsetX | (bits 8–11 of cameraOffsetY << 4); $0B11 = the same for cameraBoundsX/Y. Their consumer is not in this file.

Entry byte 9 bit 7 marks a save warp: when set it is cleared in warpFacing and the entry+4 pointer and bank are also stored in sceneSaveData ($0AF0/$0AF2), the reload point for a real game over. Both paths return carry set.
FillCollisionFromLayer0: Rebuild the collision layer ($7F:C000 = collisionLayer) from layer 0's metatile map. [$3E] = $7F:$06AA is the per-metatile flag table written by BuildMetatileFlagTable (page-aligned, one byte per metatile index). Cell count = mapRowStrideL0 x $0697 (Multiply8x8Unsigned). For each cell: the metatile index byte at $7E:A000+i replaces the low byte of $3E, and the flag byte [$3E] is stored to $7F:2000+X = $7F:C000+i when X starts at mapTilemapBaseA ($A000).
FillHorizTilemapSeg:
Inner loop that expands metatile indices into VRAM tilemap entries for a horizontal run of metatiles (a ROW strip segment; used by RenderRowStrip).

Reads $0E consecutive metatile index bytes from map data (pointed to by Y=$04). For each byte: masks to 8 bits, multiplies by 8 (ASL ×3) to index into the tile definition table at $02+offset. Copies 4 words (8 bytes) from the tile definition — the four 8×8 tile entries that compose one 16×16 metatile — into the staging buffer:
- Words 0,1 → buffer+$02/+$04 (top-left, top-right)
- Words 2,3 → buffer+$42/+$44 (bottom-left, bottom-right)

The +$42 offset places the bottom row exactly one VRAM tilemap row (32 entries × 2 bytes = 64 bytes = $40) below the top row. X advances by 4 bytes (2 entries) per metatile.
FillVertTilemapSeg:
Inner loop that expands metatile indices into VRAM tilemap entries for a vertical run of metatiles (a COLUMN strip segment; used by RenderColumnStrip).

Reads $0E consecutive metatile index bytes from map data, advancing the source Y pointer by $10 (16 bytes = one map row) per iteration to traverse vertically through the map.

For each metatile byte: masks to 8 bits, multiplies by 8 to index the tile definition table. Copies 4 tile entries to the staging buffer in a column-oriented layout:
- Words 0,2 → buffer+$02/+$04 (left column, top and bottom)
- Words 1,3 → buffer+$44/+$46 (right column, top and bottom)

The buffer holds two tile columns of 32 words each: the left column's data at +$02 (after its VRAM address word at +0) and the right column's data at +$44 (after its own VRAM address word at +$42). X advances by 4 bytes (two words per tile column) per metatile.
FindCurrentScene: Locate the current scene's command block in script data. Starts at Y=0, reads the low scene-ID byte at [$3A],Y, skips the high ID byte (u16 little-endian layout), and compares A to sceneCurrent. On match, returns with Y at the first command opcode. On mismatch, scans forward: reads each opcode and advances Y by operand size using a fall-through INY cascade ($02/$14/$15 = +1, $13 = +2, $0E = +3, $06 = +4, $11 = +5, $04/$10 = +6, $03/$05 = +7). Repeats until the target scene is found.
FindSlopeForEastMove: Slope probe used by DispatchEastMove; mirror of FindSlopeForWestMove. ProbeCurrentTR positions the probe pixels (result discarded), $1A is moved -8, then the corner sample; transition type $06 also checks the cell one row up for $05; then one row down, then ProbeFutureTR and ProbeFutureBR. Returns Z set when found (carry clear = $0A, set = $05), Z clear when none.
FindSlopeForWestMove: Slope probe used by DispatchWestMove. ProbeCurrentTL positions the probe pixels (its own result is discarded), then $1A is moved +8 and TileProbeMain samples the corner. Types: $0A or $05 end the routine at once; $09 (transition tile) also checks the cell one row up for $0A; then the cell one row down ($0A or $05), then ProbeFutureTL and ProbeFutureBL. Returns Z set when a slope was found (carry clear = $0A, set = $05) and Z clear when none.
FineAdjustXEast: X correction for the $06 / right-foot case. n = left-edge offset in its column (16 when flush). If n + $02 <= 16 only ApplyMovementDeltas runs. Otherwise $02 becomes 16 - $02, the left edge is set to (column line, one column back when flush) | $02, and $22 = (left edge + 8) << 2. Because 16 - $02 < n in that branch, the net movement is WEST by n + $02 - 16 pixels (away from a wall under the right foot), not east as the old header said. $02 can reach $1F; above $10 the subtraction goes negative and the ORA produces a wrapped X. FineAdjustXWest handles that range (it subtracts 16); this routine does not (OQ-I033-1).
FineAdjustXWest: X correction for the $09 / left-foot case. m = 16 - n (distance to the next column line east, 16 when flush). If m + $02 <= 16 only ApplyMovementDeltas runs. Otherwise $02 is re-derived through ORA #$FFF0 / EOR #$FFFF / INC (equal to $02 for 1-16, $02 - 16 above that), the left edge is set to (column line | $02) and $22 = (left edge + 8) << 2: net movement EAST by $02 - n pixels (away from a wall under the left foot). Handles $02 > 16, which FineAdjustXEast does not.
FlushDirtyTilemapStrips:
V-Blank routine that DMA-transfers all staged tilemap strips to VRAM.

Called during the NMI handler after scroll updates have been computed. Sets up common DMA registers: VMAIN=$81 (word-access, 32-word increment for column-mode), DMAP0=$01 (two-register), source bank=$7E.

Processes four staging buffer slots in order:
1. Column strip, layer 0 ($06B2 → $7E3100): DMA via DmaColumnStrip
2. Column strip, layer 1 ($06B4 → $7E3288): DMA via DmaColumnStrip
3. Row strip, layer 0 ($06B6 → $7E3184): DMA via DmaRowStrip (VMAIN switched to $80 for sequential access)
4. Row strip, layer 1 ($06B8 → $7E330C): DMA via DmaRowStrip
(The $06B2/$06B4 and $06B6/$06B8 pairs are the pointers initialised by system_init. "Horizontal"/"Vertical" in the routine names refers to the scroll direction that produces the strip, not to its shape.)

Each slot is skipped (BEQ) if its VRAM address word is zero (no pending update). After all transfers, clears all four staging buffer VRAM address words and the related staging areas to prevent re-triggering.
FlushVramWriteQueue:
Write queued tile updates to VRAM during VBlank.

1. Queued mode (dmaSkipFlag nonzero): saves SP, sets SP = $07FF so the first PLA reads word $0800 (dmaSkipFlag itself, the first queued VRAM address). Pops address/tile pairs (PLA → VMADDL, PLA → VMDATAL) until a zero address word, then restores SP and clears dmaSkipFlag.

2. Direct mode (dmaSkipFlag zero): VMAIN = $80 (word access, increment after the high byte). If $0902 (tileQueryResult) is nonzero it is the VRAM address of the top row of a 2×2 metatile: tile words $0904/$0906 go there, then $090A/$090C go to the address in $0908. $0902 is cleared afterwards (it is also cleared when it was already zero).
FreedanAttackPaletteFX: Freedan charge-up tint. Bundle #4B is 14 one-frame strips on the same 15 colors with holds 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,5,4,3,2,1,0,0 (50 ticks per pass), played twice; bundle #2C (holds mostly 0, 16 ticks per pass) repeats until the actor is killed.
FreezeCameraForAttack: Called from attack_ability_system before Psycho Dash and run attack paths: clears bit $0100 in the player actor flags and sets layerPriorityFlag bit $0200 so camera_scroll_controller stops scrolling, then falls through into RunAttackFlagSetup.
GraphicsCacheLookup: Search the 4-entry graphics cache at $0084–$008F for a matching source address. Each entry is 3 bytes (addr lo/hi, bank). Compares $3E then $40; X steps 0, 3, 6, 9. Returns carry set if found, carry clear if not.
GraphicsCacheStore: Store current source pointer ($3E/$40) into the graphics cache ring buffer. Reads ring index $0094, increments with wrap (AND #$0003), computes slot offset (index×3 via ASL+ADC), writes address and bank to $0084+X.
GridCursorDown: Grid cursor down. Consumes Down, Left and Right ($0700), SFX #10, $22 + 4 with AND $000F wrapping.
GridCursorUp: Grid cursor up. Consumes Up, Left and Right ($0B00), SFX #10, $22 − 4 with AND $000F wrapping. Shared by Arrange/Discard through the PEA/RTS trick; returns with RTS.
HandleChestInteraction:
Detect and process treasure chest interactions.

Open the chest in front of the player (called by CheckWarpAndChest each frame; see the block note for the full flow).

Guards (all must pass, else RTS):
1. layerPriorityFlag bit $0200 clear (field interaction not disabled)
2. Player actor ($09AA) flags $10 bit 2 ($0004) set: solid contact this frame, i.e. the player is pushing against a solid tile
3. joypadCurrent bit $0800 set (D-pad up)
4. GetPlayerFacingDirection == 1 (north)

Chest detection: the tile in front of the player is X = round((pos X − 8) / 16), Y = (pos Y − $20) >> 4. $F8 = chest bottom-left, $F9 = chest bottom-right (then the left neighbour must be $F8 and the origin X is decremented), anything else returns.

Record search: walks the scene's scene_chest_table records comparing bytes 0/1 with the origin; no match shows dialogstring_01FF48 ("The jewel box is tightly closed.").

Matched record, by byte 2: nonzero = item chest (displayModeFlags bit 7 set, open tiles drawn, GiveItemToPlayer; success shows dialogstring_01FF2D with SFX #$2A, or spawns ChestOpeningActor when byte 3 bit 7 is set; inventory full shows GiveItemToPlayer's Y string and redraws the closed tiles with no flag); zero = flag-only chest ("It is empty!", dialogstring_01FF36). The event flag set is byte 3 AND $7F.
HandleEmptyGeometry: Handle scenes with empty (uncompressed/zero-size) map geometry. Computes map byte count from $01×$03 via Multiply8x8Unsigned into $0666/$0667. For each active layer flag: DMAs raw map data via WriteMapBounds/DmaRomToWram. Layer 0 → $7E:A000; layer 1 only → $7E:C000; both layers → layer 0 first, then copies primary to overlay at $C000 and stores effectBoundsX/Y from map dimensions.
HideAllItemSlots: Hide all 16 item slot actors. Guard: if DP $10 bit $1000 is NOT set, returns (already hidden). Otherwise clears $1000 and walks the slot actor linked list, SETTING $2000 on each actor (making them invisible).
HideStatusActors: Hide 4 status actors by walking linked list (moveXAlt → moveYAlt → $0006,Y × 3). Sets $2000 on each. Correctly named.
InitHardwareRegisters: Boot only (SystemInit). Walks PpuRegisterInitTable: 3-byte entries [register address word, value byte] until a negative address, writing each value with STA $0000,Y (DBR = $81). It covers only the registers listed in the table (not every PPU register); the last entry, MEMSEL = 0, turns FastROM timing off again.
InitSystemVariables: Boot only (SystemInit). Zeroes all WRAM except the stack page $0100-$01FF with three DmaFixedByteFill passes ($1FF00 bytes in total; see the block note), then copies the 34 word entries of SystemInitConstants to their destinations (negative destination ends the table).
InitWarpTable:
Initialize warp table pointers for the current scene.

Reads the scene index ($0646) to look up the warp data pointer from scene_warps. Stores the pointer to $00D4 (standard warp table start).

Then walks the standard warp entries to find the extended table: each entry starts with a non-$FF byte, and the routine advances by 12 bytes ($000C) per entry until finding the $FF terminator. The byte after the terminator is stored to $00D6 (extended warp table start).
InterleaveTilesPriority: Deinterleave planar SNES 4bpp tiles into priority-split VRAM format. Sets data bank $7E, calls BuildAttributeTable, then processes $2000 bytes from $7000 in 8-byte chunks (one tile row per inner loop). For each of 8 pixel rows, ROL-cascades four bitplanes plus a per-pixel attribute bit from the lookup table into interleaved bytes at $7E:A000. Finishes with a $4000-byte DMA from $7E:A000 to VRAM $0000 via VMDATAH (mode $00, VMAIN=$80).
InventoryMainLoop: Main menu event loop. Draws the BG3 tab bar and info strings, resets the blink counter ($1C = 0), sets the last-handled-tab tracker ($18 = $FFFF, so the first pass always runs a hover preview), consumes the confirm bit ($8000) and yields. Each frame it polls TabSelectionLoop: carry set (A pressed) → TabConfirmDispatch; otherwise, if inventoryTabIndex differs from $18, the new tab is stored and its hover preview runs through SwitchCase on TabHoverDispatch; if the tab is unchanged the RTL only ends this frame's turn (it does not close the menu; TabCancel's exit flag does).
InventoryMenuDef: Actor-def wrapper for the inventory menu. Declares the actor definition header (#00, #00, #28) and contains InventoryMenuInit as the inline entry point.
InventoryMenuInit: Initialize the inventory menu. Draws the first BG3 strings, spawns 16 InventorySlotActors in a loop (counter $24 = 15→0, so the last one spawned, slot 0, heads the actor chain because SpawnAfter inserts directly after the spawner), each given its item ID as sprite frame. Saves that head to orbitAngle. Spawns EquipCursorActor (orbitDiameter), EquippedItemDisplay (moveXAlt) and the three StatusCharRow actors (moveYAlt = the last one spawned, the top row). Positions the equip cursor at inventoryEquippedIndex, yields once, then resets inventoryTabIndex to 0 (the 16 slot actors used it as their spawn counter during that yield) and sets DP $10 bit $1000 (item slots visible).
InventorySlotActor: Per-slot item display actor. Increments inventoryTabIndex (spawn counter), calls ComputeSlotPosition for screen placement. Main loop: if $28 = 0 (empty) → set $2000 (hide) and yield. If nonzero → clear $2000 (show), animate until $2A triggers.
IsMusicPlaying: Query routine: carry set while a jingle/melody sequence is active, carry clear otherwise. Active means musicTransitionState is nonzero (SPC transfer in progress) or displayModeFlags bit 7 ($0080) is set (display-filter mode, set by the MusicAndText callers and melody items until MusicLoadCleanup clears it). Called by melody items, GlobalInputHandler and several NPC scripts to avoid overlapping music or input.
IsMusicPlayingYes: Shared exit of IsMusicPlaying that returns carry set: a music transfer is in progress or the display-filter flag is still set.
JoypadToVelocity:
Convert D-pad state to packed velocity vector.

Reads joypad high byte ($0657) in 8-bit mode. Scans D-pad bits in priority order: Left ($02) > Right ($01) > Up ($08) > Down ($04). For diagonal combinations (two D-pad bits), generates reduced-magnitude velocity (±6 instead of ±8) for normalized diagonal speed.

Returns 16-bit packed result: high byte = NS (Y) velocity, low byte = EW (X) velocity.
Cardinal: ±8 sub-pixels (2.0 px/frame). Diagonal: ±6 sub-pixels (1.5 px/frame ≈ cardinal/√2).
Signs: positive X = East, negative X = West, positive Y = South, negative Y = North.
Load4bppPage: Load a full 4bpp tile page ($4000 bytes) to VRAM starting at $2000. Reads optional compressed pointer from [$3E]; if non-zero, decompresses via QuintetLZ to $7000 and uses that as source. DMA uses mode $00 (byte write), B-bus $19 (VMDATAH), size $4000 — high-byte-first 4bpp VRAM layout.
LoadScriptPointer: Read a 3-byte ROM pointer from the script stream into address X. Stores 16-bit word to $0000,X and bank byte to $0002,X, then applies SNES LoROM mapping: banks $00–$6F get +$80; banks $80–$9F additionally get +$20 with address bit 15 cleared (HiROM canonical form).
LookupEventBlock:
Look up an event block entry from the event_block_table.

Entry: A = event block index (0-based). Multiplied by 8 (ASL×3) to compute the table offset, stored to $A8 for later row-reset use.

Validation: Reads byte 0 (scene ID) from event_block_table and compares against sceneCurrent. Returns carry set (SEC) if the scene doesn't match.

On match: Switches direct page to $0000 and loads all 7 parameter bytes from the table entry into DP variables in 8-bit mode:
  Byte 7 → $A4 (layer flag)
  Bytes 5-6 → $9A/$9C (destination X/Y)
  Bytes 1-2 → $96/$98 (source X/Y)
  Byte 3 → $A2 and $9E (width, stored twice for reset)
  Byte 4 → $A0 (height)

Restores DP, returns carry clear (CLC) on success.
LzReadBitField:
Read 8 bits from the compressed bitstream and return in A.

Tests the current bit position ($72 mask) via a cascade of ASL+BMI checks; the cascade finds which bit of the mask is set, i.e. how many bits (k = 0–7) of the current source byte are already consumed.

Fast path (mask $80, k = 0, byte-aligned): reads the source byte directly via LDA [$3E], advances the pointer, returns — no shifting.

Slow path (k = 1–7): reads a 16-bit word from the source (two consecutive bytes), XBAs it to b0:b1 and ASLs it k times (the entry point into the fall-through cascade selects k: mask $40 = 1 shift ... mask $01 = 7 shifts). The high byte then holds the remaining bits of b0 followed by the top k bits of b1. Advances the source pointer by one byte, XBAs to extract that byte and returns in 8-bit mode. The mask is unchanged: 8 bits consumed leave the bit position where it was.
LzReadNibble:
Read 4 bits (a nibble) from the compressed bitstream and return in A (the back-reference copy length before the +2).

Two strategies keyed on the mask:

High path (mask >= $10: at least 5 bits left in the current byte, so the nibble fits): LSR the mask 4 times to consume 4 positions and store it. The source byte and the new mask are packed into one 16-bit word (byte in the high half, mask in the low half) and LSR shifts that word right until the mask's one-hot bit falls into carry (1–4 shifts, the shift count the nibble needs); the nibble is the low 4 bits of the high byte after XBA and AND #$0F. The source pointer does not advance.

Low path (mask < $10: 4 or fewer bits left): the nibble may straddle the byte boundary. Mask $08 = exactly 4 bits left: low nibble of the current byte, mask reset to $80, pointer advanced. Mask $04 = 3 bits left + 1 from the next byte (next mask $40, one ASL), mask $02 = 2 + 2 (next mask $20, two ASLs), mask $01 = 1 + 3 (next mask $10, three ASLs); the byte pair is read as a word, XBA'd, shifted left, and the pointer advances.

All paths return the nibble in A with AND #$0F masking.
MapCellDown:
Navigate the map index at $00 to the cell one row below (next row).

Adds $10 to the low byte (row step within page). On carry (row overflow), adds mapRowStrideL0 to the high byte (advance to next page row). Returns new index in X. Equivalent to MapIndexMoveDown in map_coords.asm.
MapCellLeft:
Navigate the map index at $00 to the cell one column to the left (previous column).

Decrements the low byte. If the low nibble underflows to $F (AND #$0F = $0F), decrements the high byte and subtracts $F0. Returns new index in X. Equivalent to MapIndexMoveLeft in map_coords.asm.
MapCellRight:
Navigate the map index at $00 to the cell one column to the right (next column).

Increments the low byte. If the low nibble wraps to zero (BIT #$0F = 0), increments the high byte and adds $F0 to compensate for page boundary crossing. Returns new index in X. Equivalent to MapIndexMoveRight in map_coords.asm.
MapCellUp:
Navigate the map index at $00 to the cell one row above (previous row).

Subtracts $10 from the low byte. On borrow, subtracts mapRowStrideL0 from the high byte (retreat to previous page row). Returns new index in X. Reverse of MapCellDown.
MapIndexMoveDown: Steps the index in $02 one row down for layer 0: low byte + $10; on carry adds mapRowStrideL0 to the page byte. Stores in $02 and returns it in X. 4 callers.
MapIndexMoveDown_L1: Same as MapIndexMoveDown with mapRowStrideL1. The initial LDA $02 has no REP, so it uses the caller's accumulator width (both callers, in event_blocks, have M = 16). Stores in $02 and returns it in X.
MapIndexMoveLeft: Steps the index in $02 one cell west (column nibble - 1; on underflow the page byte - 1 and the low byte - $F0). Returns the result in X only: unlike MapIndexMoveRight and Down it does NOT store it back in $02. 1 caller (warps_interaction chest check).
MapIndexMoveRight: Steps the index in $02 one cell east: increments the column nibble, and when it wraps (page boundary) increments the page byte and adds $F0 to restore the column. Stores the result in $02 and returns it in X. 11 callers (warps_interaction, event_blocks).
MovingEastWest:
Inertial east-west movement handler — entered when player has residual EW speed.

Entered from PlayerIdleEntry when playerSpeedEw is nonzero but no matching D-pad input. Two sub-states based on speed sign: positive → east-facing sprite (#0F), negative → west-facing (#0E). Each frame: animate, check for speed zeroing → restore saved ptr; check for direction reversal → switch sprite; check for Psycho Slider (running slide attack); check speed threshold for melee attack; check L/R for block transition.

Mirrors MovingNorthSouth for the vertical axis.
MovingNorthSouth:
Inertial north-south movement handler — entered when player has residual NS speed.

Same structure as MovingEastWest but for vertical axis. Positive → south-facing sprite (#0C), negative → north-facing (#0D). Checks up/down D-pad for direction reversal and attack transitions.
MulDivide:
Multiply then divide with the hardware registers: (A low × Y) ÷ A high.

Input: A = packed operand (low byte = multiplier, high byte = divisor), Y = 16-bit multiplicand.
Algorithm: P1 = A low × Y low and P2 = A low × Y high (two 8×8 multiplies). The dividend is the 16-bit value P1 + (P2 low byte << 8): the carry out and P2's high byte are discarded, so only the low 16 bits of A low × Y are divided. The divisor is A high; WRDIVB triggers the divide.
Output: 16-bit quotient in A (RDDIVL/RDDIVH). Divisor 0 returns $FFFF (hardware behaviour).
Timing: 3 NOPs after the multiplies (plus the instructions between), 8 NOPs (16 cycles) after the divide.
Multiply8x8Unsigned:
8×8 multiply through long-address hardware registers (named Multiply8x8Unsigned, but the $4202/$4203 multiplier is unsigned).

Input: A low = first operand, A high = second operand (8-bit accumulator). STA $80:4202, XBA, STA $80:4203.
Output: 16-bit product in A (high byte from $80:4217 via XBA, low byte from $80:4216).
Long addresses make it independent of the current data bank.
MusicJingleActor:
Jingle sequence actor started by COP MusicAndText. Saves musicParentActor (the scene's current music index) in orbitAngle, spawns SpcTransferMusicData to upload the jingle (chatPtr = $26 + 1), masks the joypad ($FFFC into joypadMaskStd) and yields each frame until musicTransitionState == $FFFF.

Then spawns MusicRenderSync (receives the string pointer $20/$22) and polls APUIO1 for $FF (the SPC700 replied). On reply it unmasks the joypad, spawns a second SpcTransferMusicData whose chatPtr is the saved scene music (so the scene track resumes), waits again for $FFFF and WaitByte(1), then falls through into MusicLoadCleanup.

Actor pool exhaustion ($1FC0 from SpawnAfterFlags) branches to MusicLoadCleanup.
MusicJingleAfterSpawn: Continuation after the first SpcTransferMusicData spawn: gives the child the jingle's music data index ($26 + 1 as chatPtr), sets $1000 in its $12 so it still runs in display-filter mode, masks the joypad (joypadMaskStd bits 2-15) and yields with SetEntryHere. On resume it polls musicTransitionState and continues at MusicJingleRenderSync once the value is $FFFF (upload complete).
MusicJingleRenderSync: Runs after the jingle upload finished: spawns MusicRenderSync (with $1000 set in its $12) and hands it the dialogue string pointer ($20) and bank ($22), then yields and polls APUIO1 every frame. The value $FF (the SPC700's reply that its sound engine is ready) continues at MusicJingleSpcReady.
MusicJingleSpcReady: After the SPC reply: unmasks the joypad again, spawns a second SpcTransferMusicData whose chatPtr is the scene music index saved in orbitAngle (so the scene track is reloaded) and polls musicTransitionState; at $FFFF it continues at MusicJingleWaitFinal. Pool exhaustion branches to MusicLoadCleanup.
MusicJingleWaitFinal: Final step of the jingle sequence: waits one frame (COP WaitByte #01), then falls through into MusicLoadCleanup, which leaves display-filter mode and kills the actor.
MusicLoadCleanup: Music actor cleanup on failure or completion. Clears displayModeFlags bit 7 ($0080: display-filter mode set by the MusicAndText caller, which froze all actors not flagged $1000) and kills the actor via COP [Die].
