Reached when SpawnAfterFlags returns $1FC0 (actor pool exhausted) or by falling through from the end of MusicJingleActor.
MusicRenderSync: One-shot actor that shows the MusicAndText string. Waits $48 (72) frames via COP [WaitByte], clears its own $1000 flag, zeros joypadMaskStd to unmask input, sets DBR to the string bank ($22), then calls UpdateFrameRender and DialogStringRenderer (Y = string pointer from $20) and dies. It was given $20/$22 by MusicJingleActor.
NorthInteractTile: Type $02 ladder ahead while moving north (a local label inside DispatchNorthMove). CheckSubTileAlignX: X straddling (carry set) -> blocked path. X flush: the player actor's entry becomes LadderClimbSouth (the ladder state entered from below: it checks Up before Down, then LadderIdleNorth) and $0008 = 0; then the blocked path runs, which holds the player at the ladder base.
NorthProbeRedirect: Entry from DispatchNorthMove when the future TL is $09 (X flush) or the east cell is $09. MapCellDown + ReadCollisionNibble here are dead (the result is unused and the BRA target's MapCellLeft starts from $00), so it simply joins the NorthWallHandler gap chain at loc_02D208 with the cell in $00 (OQ-I039-4).
NorthSlopeLeft: Current TL $0C while moving north. Same gate and flag logic as NorthSlopeRight, but with d < 8 the move is applied without touching the accumulator; otherwise the flag is set and the step goes through the slopeFracAccum filter (block note): the full $24 when |accum + $24| < 16, else -(|accum + $24| >> 4). For $24 = -8 the steps alternate -8 and -1 sub-pixels. UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.
NorthSlopeRight: Current TL $03 while moving north. Needs the current TR to be $03 too, else blocked path. Y flush, or the cell below also $03: set the slope flag and apply. Otherwise d = 16 - n (see the block note): d < 8 applies the move without the flag, d >= 8 sets $09AF bit $10 first. The direction of the slope is undecoded (OQ-I033-3).
NorthWallHandler: Current TR $09 while moving north. Current BL $09 too: ClearMovementDeltas. Otherwise ProbeFutureTR + CheckSubTileAlignY. Y straddling and future TR $09: gap chain (loc_02D208): the west cell and the cell below it must both be type 0, else ClearSpeedNS_2; both empty: ComputeYSnapOffset + FineAdjustXEast (X moves WEST). Y flush or another type: SnapXEastCollision (X floored to its column centre, west), re-probe; $09 -> slide, else zero $24 + SnapYSouthCollision + apply.
NudgeToLowerGrid:
Nudge a sub-pixel position toward the lower 16-pixel grid line ($40 sub-pixels).

Adds 8 to the position at [$00+X]. XORs old and new values — if bit 6 changed (crossed a $40 boundary), snaps to the boundary via AND $FFC0. This ensures the nudge doesn't overshoot into the next grid cell.

X register selects which position to nudge ($22 for X sub-pixel, $26 for Y sub-pixel).
NudgeToUpperGrid:
Nudge a sub-pixel position toward the upper 16-pixel grid line ($40 sub-pixels).

Subtracts 8 from the position at [$00+X]. XORs old and new — if bit 6 changed (crossed a $40 boundary upward), snaps to the next $40 boundary above via AND $FFC0 + ADC $0040. Handles the case where the subtraction would undershoot by checking BIT $003F (non-zero means not already at boundary).
OpenInventoryScreen: Open / run / close in one JSL (steps in the block note). PHP / PLP bracket the whole routine; A, X and Y are clobbered. The four words pushed in step 3 stay on the stack until step 12, so nothing between them may leave an unbalanced push.
OverlayCollisionFromLayer1: Overlay layer 1's collision flags onto the same collision layer. Same structure as FillCollisionFromLayer0 but with the flag table at $06AC, mapRowStrideL1 x $0699 cells, start index from word $0080 (= $C000 via wram-init, equal to mapTilemapBaseB) and stores through animScratch ($7F:0000+X), which for X >= $C000 is again $7F:C000+i. Zero flag bytes are skipped so layer 0's collision value survives where layer 1 has nothing.
PixelToVramAddress: DP $1A = pixel X, $1E = pixel Y. Returns A = VRAM word address in the BG1 nametable (64x32 words at $1000): row (Y and $F8) x 4, column (X and $F8) / 8, plus $0400 when X bit 8 is set. Callers: cop_handlers_metatile.ResolveTileData and two sites in event_blocks (one adds $0800 for BG2).
PlaceOpenedChestTiles:
Redraw already-opened chests into the tile map when a scene is built.

Walks the scene's records in scene_chest_table (the scene index at $0646 selects the list). Each 4-byte record is: byte 0 = X tile (bit 7 set = end of list), byte 1 = Y tile of the chest's bottom row, byte 2 = contents (item ID, 0 = flag-only), byte 3 = event flag in bits 0–6 (bit 7 = open with the music fanfare).

For each record the event flag (byte 3 AND $7F, TestEventFlag_0200) is tested. If it is set the chest was opened, so the open 2×2 pattern is written to mapLayerTilemap:
  $FE at (X, Y−1), $FF at (X+1, Y−1): top row
  $FC at (X, Y), $FD at (X+1, Y): bottom row
MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown step between the four cells. Only the tile map is written (no VRAM update).
PlayerCharacterDef:
Player character actor definition table and initialization code.

The actor-def header (#00, #08, #85) defines the actor type. The inline init code:
1. Sets $0100 in actor flags $10 and $0001 in $12 (meaning of both bits: OQ-I025-1)
2. Stores the current actor slot as playerActor ($09AA)
3. Sets the free101C marker to signal the player actor is active
4. Checks the game-over wakeup flag ($0AF8) — spawns DeathWakeupMessage if set
5. Spawns four companion actors: attack_ability_system (SpawnBefore), player_move_controller and slope_ramp_physics (SpawnAfter), shadow_shimmer (SpawnListAppend, flags $2800)

These companions handle combat, physics, slope detection, and Shadow's palette shimmer respectively. The player character actor itself handles only the movement state machine.
PlayerIdleDispatchTable:
7-entry × 4-direction idle dispatch table (28 entries, 56 bytes).

Indexed by (facing × 7 + input_priority). Each row of 7 entries: [Attack, WalkEast, WalkWest, WalkSouth, WalkNorth, Block, IdleStand]. The facing direction determines which row is used, and the input scan priority determines the column.
PlayerIdleEntry:
Main idle state entry and input dispatch loop.

Clears transient state: the D-pad bits of joypadHeld ($F0FF mask, so held directions are re-detected), playerFlags $2800 (block and script/ability lock), actor flag $0020 (the block marker) and climbStateData; sets actor flag $0100 again. Returns at once when bit $2000 of actor flags $10 is set (SortActorsByDepth treats that bit as hidden; who sets it on the player is OQ-I025-2).

Saves itself as the return point via SetSavedPtr, clears force movement. Checks for residual speed — if nonzero, jumps to MovingEastWest or MovingNorthSouth for inertial deceleration.

If no residual speed, computes a dispatch index: GetPlayerFacing (0=S, 1=N, 2=W, 3=E, also left in $24) × 14 via Multiply8x8Unsigned → row offset into PlayerIdleDispatchTable. Then scans joypadCurrent in priority order: attack button > D-pad cardinal (S/N/W/E) > L/R block > idle stand. The resulting 2-byte address is loaded from the table and executed via the DEC+PHA+RTS trick.
PlayerMoveController:
Per-frame player movement integration — SpawnAfter companion actor.

Seven-stage pipeline executed every frame after the player character:
1. SUBPIXEL SCALING: Local coords ($14,$16) × 4 for 2-bit fractional precision (0.25 px resolution)
2. FREEZE CHECK: Skip if actor flag $0080 (freeze) set AND iframeCounter non-negative
3. SCRIPT/GAME-OVER GATE: If playerFlags $0A00 ($0200 game over + $0800 script/ability lock), zero external velocities and skip
4. POSITION SYNC: If local position differs from player actor (teleported), re-sync
5. VELOCITY CALC: Combine joypad D-pad velocity (from JoypadToVelocity) OR speed × 4 with external velocity ($0408/$040A). Attack/block flags ($3000) force zero joypad velocity
6. COLLISION: Grounded ($0008) → PlayerMovementTick (full tile collision). Airborne → direct position add
7. WRITEBACK: Store sub-pixel and pixel positions back to actor, sync flag bit 2 (solid contact)

External velocities (wind, conveyors, knockback) are consumed each frame — sources must re-apply them every frame to persist.
PlayerMovementTick:
Per-frame grounded player movement dispatch with collision.

Entry: X = player actor DP offset (stored to $000A). Called by player_move_controller when the player is grounded (flag $0008).

Two-phase processing:

Phase 1 (EW/diagonal): Reads DP $20 (horizontal velocity). Saves $24 (vertical velocity) to stack, zeroes $24 and $AA (collision flags). Clears player actor flag $0004 (solid contact). Dispatches based on $20 sign: negative → DispatchWestMove (with $0040 diagonal flag), positive → DispatchEastMove (with $0040). After dispatch, converts sub-pixel positions ($22, $26) back to pixel (>>2) and stores to player actor $0014/$0016.

Phase 2 (NS): Restores $24 from stack. Negative → DispatchNorthMove (skipped if $AA bit $0800 set = south wall). Positive → DispatchSouthMove (skipped if $AA bit $0400 set = east wall).

DP is set to $0000 during movement calculations. Player actor pointer X is saved and restored via PHX/PLX.
PositionEquipCursor: Position equip cursor at slot $1A. If $1A ≥ 0: same grid math as PositionGridCursor. If $1A < 0: hides cursor (ORA $2000).
PositionGridCursor: Position a grid cursor actor from a slot index: primary entry uses $22 / actor $20. After slot × 4, bits 2–3 select the column (stride 4 into GridColumnPositions) and bits 4–5 select the row ($0030 mask = row × $10, added to the base Y). Writes $0014/$0016. The second entry loc_02EA46 (source cursor $2E / $2C) has no caller.
PpuRegisterInitTable: 76 register writes of [address word, value byte] terminated by a negative address. Order: MDMAEN, HDMAEN, then the PPU registers $2100-$2133 in address order (write-twice registers appear twice), then NMITIMEN, WRIO, the multiply/divide inputs, H/V timers and finally MEMSEL = 0. Selected values: INIDISP $80, OBJSEL $02, BGMODE $09, BG1SC $11, BG2SC $19, BG3SC $78, BG12NBA $22, BG34NBA $06, VMAIN $80, M7SEL $80, windows $33 / WH1 $FF, TM $04, CGWSEL $82, COLDATA $E0, NMITIMEN 0, WRIO $FF.
ProbeCurrentBL:
Probe the bottom-left corner of the player's hitbox at current position.

X pixel = $22 >> 2 − 8 (left edge), Y pixel = $26 >> 2 − 1 (bottom edge). Calls TileProbeMain. Post-probe: INC $1E (→ 0). Returns carry set if collision detected.
ProbeCurrentBR:
Probe the bottom-right corner of the player's hitbox at the current position.

X pixel = $22 >> 2 + 7 (right edge), Y pixel = $26 >> 2 - 1 (bottom edge); calls TileProbeMain; afterwards INC $1A (+8) and INC $1E (bottom + 1) place the stored coordinates one pixel past the right and bottom edges, so that CheckSubTileAlignX/Y report whether those edges are flush with a tile boundary (MapCell steps use the index in $00, not these pixels). Carry set when the type is nonzero.
ProbeCurrentTL:
Probe the top-left corner of the player's hitbox at current position.

X pixel = $22 >> 2 − 8 (left edge), Y pixel = $26 >> 2 − 16 (top edge). Calls TileProbeMain. No post-probe adjustment. Returns carry from TileProbeMain directly (nonzero collision type = carry set).
ProbeCurrentTR:
Probe the top-right corner of the player's hitbox at current position.

X pixel = $22 >> 2 + 7 (right edge), Y pixel = $26 >> 2 − 16 (top edge). Calls TileProbeMain. Post-probe: INC $1A (→ +8). Returns carry set if collision detected.
ProbeFutureBL:
Probe the bottom-left corner of the player's hitbox at future position.

X pixel = ($20 + $22) >> 2 − 8, Y pixel = ($24 + $26) >> 2 − 1. Calls TileProbeMain. Post-probe: INC $1E (→ 0). Returns carry set if collision detected.
ProbeFutureBR:
Probe the bottom-right corner of the player's hitbox at future position.

X pixel = ($20 + $22) >> 2 + 7, Y pixel = ($24 + $26) >> 2 − 1. Calls TileProbeMain. Post-probe: INC $1A (→ +8), INC $1E (→ 0). Returns carry set if collision detected.
ProbeFutureTL:
Probe the top-left corner of the player's hitbox at future position.

X pixel = ($20 + $22) >> 2 − 8, Y pixel = ($24 + $26) >> 2 − 16. Calls TileProbeMain. No post-probe adjustment. Returns carry from TileProbeMain directly.
ProbeFutureTR:
Probe the top-right corner of the player's hitbox at future (post-velocity) position.

X pixel = ($20 + $22) >> 2 + 7, Y pixel = ($24 + $26) >> 2 − 16. Calls TileProbeMain. Post-probe: INC $1A (→ +8). Returns carry set if collision detected.
ProjectileSouth:
Dark Gaia fight projectile actor — south direction.

Spawned by AttackSouth only in scene $E8 (SpawnListAppend, flags $0602). Uses the spriteset_will_projectile metasprite. Two-phase animation: initial launch (sprite #00, MoveY #09), then looping travel (sprite #04, MoveY #0F). Dies when bit 14 ($4000) of its actor flags $10 is set — sprite_composition sets that bit for actors outside the screen bounds — so it flies until it leaves the screen.

North/West/East variants use matching sprite pairs and MoveX/MoveY directions.
QueueVisibleTileVram:
Queue the 2×2 metatile VRAM update for the tile at pixel position ($1A, $1E) if it is inside the camera window. Layer 0 only: X = map index of the tile in mapLayerTilemap, Y = queue offset (JSR, same bank).

Window test: (pixelX + 16 − bg1ScrollH) < $0111, and (pixelY − ((mapScrollV − 16) AND $FFF0)) in 0..$F0.

On-screen: reads the mapLayerTilemap byte, ×8 indexes metatileMapLayer ($7E2000), copies its four tile words to $0802/$0806/$080A/$080E + Y, and stores PixelToVramAddress (BG1 nametable) and the +1 / +$20 / +$21 neighbours as the four address words ($0800/$0804/$0808/$080C + Y). Y advances by $10 per metatile.

Returns: carry set = off-screen; carry clear + Z set = queue full (Y reached $0100, LDX #0 forces Z); carry clear otherwise (Z is inherited from the caller's flags, OQ-62). Also used by DrawChestTiles in warps_interaction.
QuintetLzDecompress:
Main QuintetLZ decompression routine.

Sets data bank to $7E, initializes the 256-byte dictionary ($7E0200–$02FF, shared with the depth-sort bucket array) with $20 (space), sets the dictionary write position to $EF, and enters the main decompression loop.

Main loop reads one control bit per iteration:
- Bit = 1 (literal): reads 8-bit byte via LzReadBitField, writes to both the output buffer (STA $0000,X) and dictionary (STA ($74))
- Bit = 0 (back-reference): reads 8-bit dictionary index via LzReadBitField (stored to $76), then 4-bit copy length via LzReadNibble (+2 minimum). Copies bytes from dictionary at the read position ($76) to both the output and dictionary write position ($74). Uses the XBA trick to stash the copy counter in the B register, freeing A for dictionary reads

The output counter (Y) decrements per byte written. When Y reaches zero, decompression is complete (even in the middle of a back-reference copy).

Preserves X, Y, P and the data bank via PHP/PHB/PHX/PHY at entry; A is not preserved.
RampSnapEastNorthTrWall: East ramp path when TR is blocked but BR is open: SnapYNorthCollision then ApplyMovementDeltas.
RampSnapEastSouthBrWall: East ramp post-move corner fix when future TR is passable but BR is solid: calls SnapYSouthCollision then ApplyMovementDeltas; reached from EastRampDown/EastRampUp wall probes.
RampSnapWestNorthTrWall: West ramp TR-blocked BR-open case: SnapYNorthCollision then ApplyMovementDeltas.
RampSnapWestSouthBrWall: West ramp analogue of the TR-open BR-solid case: SnapYSouthCollision then ApplyMovementDeltas from WestRampDown/WestRampUp probes.
RangedAttackSouth:
Will-only lunge follow-up — south direction.

Reached from AttackSouth when Will (form 0) holds the facing direction during the swing. Calls RangedSetForceY (force move #46, playerFlags $0800, climbStateData = 1, actor flag $0200, extendedFlags $0040), shows sprite #44, animates once, then clears actor flag $0200 and extendedFlags $0040 (AndExtraFlags #$FFBF) and restores the saved ptr.

North/West/East variants mirror this with sprites #45/#46/#47. North sets $2000 and west sets $4000 in $12, the direction-negate bits tile_collision_physics uses to flip the Y / X delta; the east and south variants need no flip. No projectile is spawned here (OQ-I025-5).
ReadCollisionNibble:
Read the collision type at map index X (8-bit A).

X >= $4000 (outside the map) returns $0F. Otherwise the byte at collisionLayer ($7FC000) + X is read: if its high nibble is nonzero (the solid mark that actors OR in with $F0) the high nibble is shifted down and returned ($F0 becomes $0F, solid); if it is zero the byte, i.e. the terrain type in the low nibble, is returned. BIT #$FF at the end sets Z when the type is 0.
ReadDecelerationStep: Return in A the curve word at decelCurvePtr + (decelStepCounter & $0F) x 2 (flags set from A: zero = no deceleration this step) and increment decelStepCounter, whether or not the word is zero. Default curve: $0001 at steps 7 and 15.
ReadDecelerationStepNS: Exact copy of ReadDecelerationStep for the NS routine: same decelStepCounter, same decelCurvePtr, same result. It could simply be a JSR to ReadDecelerationStep.
ReadScriptByte: Read one byte from the scene script stream at [$3A],Y. Saves/restores processor state, clears the B accumulator (XBA with #$00) so callers in 16-bit mode receive a clean low byte in A, advances Y, and returns.
RebuildCollisionLayer: Rebuild the collision layer after the scene script ends (skipped for scene $F7). Always runs FillCollisionFromLayer0; when scrollModeFlags bit 0 (dual-layer scene) is set, OverlayCollisionFromLayer1 overlays layer 1's flags.
ReloadAbilityFX: Re-uploads the ability effect tiles and palette after the inventory scene overwrote sprite VRAM. $00EA (activeAbilityGfx): 0 = nothing to do; 1 = misc_fx_1CC000 ($0480 bytes) to VRAM word $4400 and fx_palette_198070 (16 colours, staging colour index $A0 = OBJ palette row 10); 2 or more = misc_fx_1CC480 ($0600 bytes) to $4400 and fx_palette_198090 (7 colours from colour index $A9). The palette goes into the $7F0A00 staging buffer; the NMI upload sends it to CGRAM. The screen is still in forced blank, so the DMA is safe.
RenderColumnStrip:
Renders one COLUMN strip (a vertical run of 16 metatiles = 256px, one tile-column pair) into the column staging buffer ($06B2+X) for V-Blank DMA (DmaColumnStrip).

The most complex rendering routine. Computes the map data index from the pixel position: page = Y_page × map width in pages (Multiply8x8Unsigned) + X_page + base page, then metatile row ×16 + metatile column within the page. The tile column (X >> 3, forced even) is the VRAM word offset in the 64-wide ring; bit 5 of it selects the left or right nametable, which changes only the VRAM address ($400 higher for the right one).

The strip is filled in VRAM order (buffer row = VRAM metatile row), starting at the current Y row, in up to two segments:
1. First segment: 16 − Y_row metatiles, from the current row to the bottom of the map page
2. Second segment (only if Y_row > 0): the remaining Y_row metatiles from the top of the next page row (map width bytes further, wrapped at the map data end)

Each segment calls FillVertTilemapSeg to expand metatile indices into VRAM-format entries. Finally an edge-tile step overwrites the last slot with the metatile row just above the strip start (same VRAM ring row), stepping back a page row when the start row is 0 (inferred from the arithmetic; not runtime-verified).

The buffer holds two tile columns: [VRAM addr][32 words] at +0 and [VRAM addr+1][32 words] at +$42 (the right tile column of each 2-wide metatile).
RenderPaletteTiles: Render palette-indexed metatile map data into a $4000-byte tile buffer at $7E:B000 for VRAM upload. Zeroes output in 8-byte chunks, caps visible rows at 4 (from $0693/$0697). Triple-nested loop walks map pages and expands each metatile index through S_metatileMapLayer into four 8×8 tile words with $80-byte row stride. DMAs $4000 bytes from $B000 to VRAM $0000 (VMAIN=$00, low-byte writes), then restores VMAIN=$80.
RenderRowStrip:
Renders one ROW strip (a horizontal run of 32 metatiles = 512px, two 256px map pages) into the row staging buffer ($06B6+X) for V-Blank DMA (DmaRowStrip).

Computes the map data offset from the Y position ($1C/$1D) using the map width in pages ($0693+X, the high byte of mapBoundsX) and the tilemap base address via Multiply8x8Unsigned. The strip always starts at the left edge of a map page: the Y metatile row (×64 VRAM words) selects the VRAM row, and bit 8 of X ($18) selects which nametable receives the first page.

Always makes two passes: each calls FillHorizTilemapSeg to expand 16 metatile indices (one map page) into VRAM-format 2×2 tile entries. Between the passes the map index advances one page (+$100) and is wrapped via WrapMapIndex. The two passes use staging slot 0 and the slot at +$82, with their VRAM addresses ordered by the nametable bit.

Operates in bank $7E (data bank set via PHB) for direct access to the map and staging buffers.
ResetThinkerWaitCounters: Walks the THINKER list: DP $5A is the thinker list head ($5C the tail; the actor list uses $56 / $58). For each thinker D is set to its slot, the wait counter at $08 is zeroed (0 = run on the next pass; a stored n skips n passes) and the next-link at $06 is followed until it is zero. It runs after RestoreGameState, so it hits the restored gameplay thinkers, not leftovers of the inventory scene. D and P are saved around it.
RestoreCachedVram: Restore previously cached VRAM tile data from the WRAM ring buffer. Reads slot index from CacheSlotIndices table (X), computes WRAM source via ROR×4 + AND + ADC. If total size fits in one $2000 block, single DmaWramToVram; otherwise splits into $2000 + remainder with VRAM offset bumped ($0668 + $10) and next ring slot for the second transfer.
RestoreGameState: Reverse of SaveGameState for everything except the palette staging buffer. DP $4E-$5D comes back before the pages it points into; both are restored before anything runs. scrollOverrideV, $06CC and $00B2 are not restored because they were never saved (OQ-I034-4).
RestorePaletteBuffer: Copies $203 bytes from $7E:38B4 back to the $7F:0A00 palette staging buffer. Called after the scene graphics are reloaded so LoadScenePalettes and the ability palette see the saved colours.
RngStep_Unused:
Generator step (no callers); the same loops as the inline step in RngByte (cop_handlers_movement), without the output byte.

For X = 15..1: byte[$040F+X] += byte[$0410+X] + carry (one carry chain, $041E first). Then a ripple counter at $041F is incremented, carrying toward lower addresses until a byte does not wrap. The state array is $0410-$041F; rngState ($040F) is only the base used for the X offset.
RunAttackNS:
North-south Psycho Slider animation — Will's running slide attack along vertical axis.

Loads anim table A entry 1, sets body sprite #04. Branches by speed sign:
- South (positive): sprites #0C → #0D loop → #0E finish, zeros NS speed
- North (negative): SetForceNE, sprites #0F → #10 loop → #11 finish

Both paths: RunAttackFlagSetup (set $0200 actor flag, consume attack, set $0802 playerFlags), loop with AnimLoop for slide distance, RunAttackCleanup, restore saved ptr.
RunAttackSpeedCheck:
Route Psycho Slider to EW or NS based on which axis has sufficient speed.

Computes |playerSpeedEw| — if >= 3, pops return and jumps to RunAttackEW. Otherwise computes |playerSpeedNs| — if >= 3, pops return and jumps to RunAttackNS. If neither axis has sufficient speed, returns to caller (no slide attack).
SaveGameState: Copies the state listed in the block note's SAVE MAP into the backup areas and zeroes joypadCurrent / joypadMaskStd so no gameplay input leaks into the inventory scene. DBR is saved with PHB because every MVN leaves the destination bank in DBR. Each MVN leaves X / Y just past its block, which is why some copies reload only one of the two registers (save: X only on the second, fourth and sixth copy; restore: Y only on the second and fourth).
SaveVramToRingBuffer: Back up newly loaded VRAM tile data to the WRAM ring buffer for later cache restoration. Sets VMADDL from $0668. If size exceeds $2000, splits: first $2000 bytes via DmaVramToRam, then advances ring index (wrap at 4), invalidates that cache slot ($FFFF/$FF), offsets VMADDL by $1000, and DMAs the remainder.
scene_script_jump_table: 24-entry word jump table mapping scene opcode indices ($00–$17) to handler addresses. Unused slots ($00–$01, $07–$0D, $0F, $12, $16) point to SceneCmd_Default (RTS no-op). Active handlers: $02=ConfigDisplay, $03=LoadBgTiles, $04=LoadTilemap, $05=LoadDualTilemap, $06=FullGraphics, $0E=Skip3, $10=LoadSpriteTiles, $11=SpcMusicLoad, $13=ConditionalLoad, $14=Nop, $15=SkipScriptCommands, $17=LoadCharTiles.
SceneCmd_ConditionalLoad: Conditional script execution gate. Reads one byte (flag index) from the script stream and calls TestFlagRaw. If the flag is set (carry set), jumps to SkipScriptCommands to bypass the remaining commands in the block. If clear, advances Y past the flag operand and returns so subsequent commands execute normally.
SceneCmd_ConfigDisplay: Scene command $02: apply a display_preset_table record (10 bytes; index from script, record via pointer table). Record bytes: +0 TM and TMW, +1 TS and TSW, +2 CGWSEL, +3 CGADSUB, +4 layer flags, +5 layerPriorityFlag, +6 BGMODE, +7 scroll/HUD flags, +8/+9 unused (loaded and discarded). Byte +4: bits 4-5 -> $06F1; bit 0/1 -> tile-priority bit ($2000) OR'd into layer 0/1 tilemap entries via $06A2/$06A4; bit 6 -> visible height $06EC ($100 set, $E0 clear); bit 7 clear -> $06A5 bit 0 (+$100 tile-number offset for layer 1). Byte +5 low nibble gives BG1SC/BG2SC size bits (bit 7 swaps the $1000/$1800 bases). Byte +7: low 5 bits -> scrollModeFlags (bit 3 also invalidates the BG-tile source-cache slot $066C), bit 7 -> sets hudDisableFlag bit $40 (otherwise cleared). A changed $06A2/$06A4 invalidates tilemap source-cache slots $0678/$067B.
SceneCmd_Default: Default scene-command handler: single RTS instruction. Jump-table target for all unimplemented opcode slots; consumes no operands.
SceneCmd_FullGraphics: Complete scene graphics load — the most complex scene command. Reads flags $066A and source pointer; optionally clears layer bits on source cache hits ($067E layer 0, $0681 layer 1). Reads map width/height pairs into $00/$01 (X) and $02/$03 (Y). If no layers active after cache filtering, returns early. With active layers but zero geometry (compressed pointer $0000), HandleEmptyGeometry. With nonzero geometry: StoreMapAndDecompress per active layer; layer 1 also copies primary decompressed data from $A000 to $C000 and stores secondary map dimensions. If flags indicate no tilemap layers (AND #$7F == 0), DmaLowVramTileset loads tiles directly to low VRAM.
SceneCmd_LoadBgTiles: Scene command $03: load BG tile graphics to VRAM. Script operands: start byte, end byte (each x$200 into $0664/$0666 = byte window inside the decompressed data), VRAM page byte ($0668), 3-byte source pointer, mode byte. The mode adds a fixed VRAM word-address base to the page (0 = +$2000 via slot $066C/$066F chosen by page bit 4, 1 = +$4000 via slot $0672/$0675, 2 = +$6000 with no source-cache check, 3 = whole $4000-byte 4bpp page via Load4bppPage). CheckSourceCacheHit returning a hit ends the command. On a miss: DeinterleavePlanarTiles when layerPriorityFlag $0800 is set and slot is $066C; else GraphicsCacheLookup -> RestoreCachedVram on a VRAM-cache hit; otherwise decompress via QuintetLZ to $7E:7000, DMA through SceneDmaTileShim, then SaveVramToRingBuffer.
SceneCmd_LoadCharTiles: Load character/object tiles with flexible VRAM targeting. Reads flags $066A and source pointer; reads width×height words, Multiply8x8Unsigned, then ×8 for tile byte size in $0666. Decompresses to $7000 if compressed pointer non-null. VRAM destination from flags: bit 7 = (flags & $7F)×4 absolute address; bit 0 = $1000 (PEA+RTS chains to bit 1 check); bit 1 = $1800; neither bit → return without DMA. Transfer: mode $01, B-bus $18, size $0666.
SceneCmd_LoadDualTilemap: Load tilemaps for both BG layers from shared compressed source data. Reads three size operands (XBA + LSR×2 for >>2 scaling) plus flags byte $066A (bit 0 = layer 0, bit 1 = layer 1). Each active layer is checked against its source cache slot ($0678/$067B); cache hits clear that layer bit. If any layers remain: decompress once to $7000, then for each active layer DMA to $7E:2000 (layer 0) or $7E:2800 (layer 1) and call BuildMetatileFlagTable.
SceneCmd_LoadSpriteTiles: Load sprite tile graphics. Reads 16-bit tile data size from [$3A],Y (stores to $0666), advances Y by 3, loads source pointer. CheckSourceCacheHit on $0684 — hit returns without work. On miss: if compressed pointer non-null, decompresses to $4000; if null ($0000), DmaRomToWram from ROM to $7E:4000 (uncompressed sprite tile staging).
SceneCmd_LoadTilemap: Load tilemap data from ROM to WRAM. Reads three script operands (start, end, WRAM destination offset), each doubled (ASL) into $0664/$0666/$0668 for word addressing. Loads source pointer via LoadScriptPointer, then DmaRomToWram into $7F:0A00 + offset. Special case: destination offset $0020 (palette tilemap) copies one palette entry from $7F0A20 into cgramPalette after the DMA.
SceneCmd_Nop: No-operation scene command — advances the script pointer by one byte (INY) and returns. Used as a placeholder or padding byte in command streams.
SceneCmd_Skip3: Skip three bytes in the scene script stream (INY ×3) and return. Used for commands with a fixed 3-byte operand the engine does not interpret.
SceneDmaTileShim: Entry wrapper for DmaTileStripToVram. Saves processor state and BRA branches into DmaTileStripToVram. CheckInterleavedFlag is an alternate entry in the same block: if layerPriorityFlag bit $0800 is set, jumps to InterleaveTilesPriority for priority deinterleaving instead of a direct DMA.
SceneScriptMain: Main scene script interpreter. Saves processor state, calls FindCurrentScene to locate the current scene's command block, then enters a dispatch loop: ReadScriptByte → opcode $00 ends the scene (RebuildCollisionLayer unless sceneCurrent == $F7, then return) → otherwise index scene_script_jump_table and dispatch via the RTS trick (PEA return-1, load handler address, DEC, PHA, RTS). Script pointer lives at [$3A],Y throughout.
SceneScriptNoMusic: Variant of SceneScriptMain used when reloading scene graphics without restarting music. Same dispatch loop, but after jump-table lookup compares the handler address against SpcMusicLoadCmd — on match, skips 5 operand bytes (INY ×5) instead of executing. Does not call RebuildCollisionLayer on scene end; simply restores state and returns.
ScreenBlackout:
Set INIDISP ($2100) to $00 — brightness 0, forced blank released.

Clears bit 7 (forced blank off) and sets brightness to $0. The screen appears completely black but the PPU continues processing internally. Used to darken the display while keeping the PPU active.
SelectionCursorActor: Generic animated cursor actor. StageSprAndHitbox with sprite #40, SetEntryExit. Loop: SetEntryHere + AnimOneFrame until $2A signals update.
SetActorCollisionFlag:
Mark the current actor as having touched a solid tile this tick (flag $0004).

Y is loaded from $000A, the actor slot address that PlayerMovementTick stored there (the earlier note's 'actor ID x 2' is wrong: Y is used directly as the actor's base address). Bit $0004 of the flags word at actor + $10 is the per-tick solid-contact flag; PlayerMovementTick clears it before each collision pass.
SetAnimStatePointer:
Set an actor's function pointer and clear its frame counter.

Stores A to $0000,Y (the actor's execution pointer / animation state), then zeros $0008,Y (frame counter / animation timer). Used by ChestOpeningActor to override the player actor's animation during the chest opening sequence.
SetSlotSprite: Set actor sprite data: A → $0028,Y (frame), zero $002A,Y (anim) and $0008,Y (timer).
ShadowShimmerActive:
Palette shimmer active state — animating palette transitions.

Runs the movement palette cycling animation while the player is moving. Returns to Idle when movement stops.
ShadowShimmerIdle:
Palette shimmer idle state — waiting for player movement.

Monitors player speed for changes. When movement is detected, transitions to the Active state. When stationary, holds the current palette frame.
ShadowShimmerInit:
Shadow's palette shimmer companion actor — initialization.

SpawnLastRel companion spawned by PlayerCharacterDef. First checks characterForm — if not 2 (Shadow), immediately dies. Otherwise initializes the palette shimmer system and enters the Idle state.

Active only when the player is Shadow form, providing the distinctive shimmering palette visual effect.
ShowAllItemSlots: Show all 16 item slot actors. Guard: if DP $10 bit $1000 is already set, returns (already visible). Otherwise sets $1000 and walks the slot actor linked list (orbitAngle → $0006,Y chain × 16), CLEARING $2000 from each actor (making them visible).
ShowDialogueFrame:
Bank-1 dialogue rendering wrapper. Sets DBR to $81 (bank 1) for dialogue data access, temporarily clears joypadMaskStd to unmask all buttons during dialogue processing, calls UpdateFrameRender (one render-only frame), then calls DialogStringRenderer (the bank-1 dialogue engine) with Y still holding the string pointer. Restores joypad mask and data bank on return.

The bank switch is necessary because DialogStringRenderer reads dialogue strings DB-relative (Y = pointer) from bank $01/$81.
ShowEquipCursor: Show equip cursor (clear $2000). If nothing equipped, falls through to HideEquipCursor. Correctly named.
SkipScriptCommands: Skip a counted block of scene commands. Reads a count byte (pushed as stack boundary), then scans opcodes with the same operand-size logic as FindCurrentScene. Opcode $12 terminates immediately; nested opcode $15 compares its inner count byte against the stacked boundary — equal count ends the skip. All other opcodes advance Y by their operand size until termination.
SlopeFlatDecelerate: Flat-ground deceleration entry (also reached directly from the frozen gate and the zero-speed path). EW speed nonzero: DecelerateEW and RTL, so the NS axis is not touched on that frame. EW speed zero: clear playerFlags $1000 if it is set (the player has come to rest), then DecelerateNS if the NS speed is nonzero. RTL.
SlopeFlatExit: No slope under the player: ClampSpeeds, clear slopeFracAccum and slopeStepCounter, restore D and X (pushed in SlopePhysicsEntry) and fall straight into SlopeFlatDecelerate, which returns with RTL. There is no RTL in this block.
SlopeHandlerExit: Common tail after slope curve handlers in SlopeType0AHandler: calls ClampSpeeds, restores direct page and X from the entry save, returns with RTL.
SlopePhysicsEntry: Per-frame entry of the companion actor (see the block note for the four paths). X is saved around the player-flag gate. When the actor has speed it saves D, sets D = 0 for TileProbeMain's work area ($1A = pixel X, $1E = pixel Y, tile index in $00) and probes (actor X, actor Y - 8). The collision type, doubled, indexes SlopeTileDispatch: a nonzero entry is the handler (DEC, PHA, RTS dispatch), zero means no slope. For types $06 and $09 the cells one row below and one row above the probe tile are tested for $05 / $0A. With zero speed and the $1000 latch it clears slopeStepCounter and decelStepCounter, probes the current, right, below and below-right cells at playerXPos / playerYPos and dispatches the first slope found; otherwise it ends in SlopeFlatExit.
SlopeSpeedZeroLatch: Shared zero-speed branch from ApplySlopeCurvePosEW and NS helpers: clears slopeStepCounter, sets playerFlags bit $1000 (stopped on slope), returns with RTS to the caller.
SlopeTileDispatch: 16-word table indexed by collision type x 2. Types $03, $05, $0A and $0C hold the address of a slope handler; the rest are $0000. SlopePhysicsEntry reads it with a long-indexed LDA, then DEC, PHA, RTS dispatches (the table stores the handler address itself; the DEC makes the RTS land on it).
SlopeType03Handler: Collision type $03: apply the positive NS curve (slopeCurvePtrB) to playerSpeedNs, then ClampSpeeds, PLD, PLX, RTL. Pushes the player south.
SlopeType05Handler: Collision type $05: apply the negated EW curve (slopeCurvePtrA) to playerSpeedEw. Pushes the player west (eastward speed shrinks, westward speed grows). Shares the exit SlopeHandlerExit (ClampSpeeds, PLD, PLX, RTL) with the other three handlers.
SlopeType0AHandler: Collision type $0A: apply the positive EW curve (slopeCurvePtrA) to playerSpeedEw. Pushes the player east. The next label SlopeType0CHandler (type $0C, negated NS curve of slopeCurvePtrB, pushes north) lives inside this block; the common exit SlopeHandlerExit calls ClampSpeeds and returns with PLD, PLX, RTL.
SlotActorEvaluate: Per-frame entry for InventorySlotActor after ComputeSlotPosition: hides the slot actor when sprite frame $28 is zero, otherwise shows it and AnimOneFrame loops until refresh flag $2A is set.
SnapXEastCollision: X snap after a blocked east step: X' = (((X + $20) - 32) AND $FFC0) + 32, $20 = 0. The right edge ends flush to the wall; with $20 = 0 (callers in player_move_ns / player_move_south) it only moves X west. The full entry zeroes playerSpeedEw first; the loc_02D766 entry (after a successful Y nudge) keeps it.
SnapXWestCollision:
Snap X to the nearest tile centre after a wall hit during west movement.

Computes X = (((X + $20) - $0020) & $FFC0) + $0060 (the first $20 is the velocity at DP $20, the second the immediate constant 32 sub-pixels), then zeroes $20. Coordinates are in sub-pixels, 4 per pixel: $FFC0 rounds to a 16-pixel tile boundary and the + $60 / - $20 pair lands on the centre of the nearest tile. The SnapXWestCollision entry also zeroes playerSpeedEw; the loc_02DC16 entry (used after a successful Y nudge) keeps the speed.
SnapYNorthCollision: Y snap after a blocked north step: $26 = (($24 + $26) AND $FFC0) + $40, $24 = 0, so the hitbox top ends flush under the blocking row. The full entry zeroes playerSpeedNs first; the loc_02D0C2 entry (used after a successful AutoAlignEW nudge) keeps it. With $24 = 0 (east / west wall-slide callers) it pushes south by 1..16 px. See the block note.
SnapYSouthCollision: Hard Y snap after a south wall hit: zero playerSpeedNs, then Y = (Y + $24) AND $FFC0 (floor to a 16-pixel row line), $24 = 0. Callers outside this file reach it from the east / ns / diag dispatchers as well, with $24 already zero or not.
SoftDivide_Unused:
Software long division (no callers). Uses DP = 0 scratch $00-$06. A = divisor, Y = dividend.

The divisor is normalized by shifting left until its MSB is set (shift count in $00, normalized divisor in $02). The dividend then acts as a running remainder through two trial-subtraction loops: the first collects the integer quotient bits into $06 (shift count + 1 iterations, at most 16), the second 16 further bits into $04 (a 16.16 fixed-point quotient, inferred). Probably a development fallback before the hardware divider wrapper.
SouthBlockedWall: Wall handler for south movement: SetActorCollisionFlag, then AutoAlignEW_South. Carry clear (X nudged) enters the shared floor code at loc_02D3FD without zeroing playerSpeedNs; carry set falls into SnapYSouthCollision, which does zero it. The PHP before the BRA balances the PLP at the end of the shared code.
SouthInteractTile: Ladder reached while walking south. The hitbox must be over a single column (CheckSubTileAlignX carry clear), otherwise the tile counts as a wall. Sets the player actor's entry address ($0000,Y) to LadderClimbNorth and clears its wait counter ($0008,Y), then branches to SouthBlockedWall so the usual Y snap runs. LadderClimbNorth is the climb state entered from above (it checks Down before Up and falls to LadderIdleSouth); the name follows its entry animation, not the walking direction.
SouthSlideJumpShim: Branch shim: enters the south-wall gap test (loc_02D54C in SouthWallSouthInteract) from DispatchSouthMove when FutureBL or the cell to its right is type $06.
SouthSlopeLeft: Slope type $0C: same dispatch as SouthSlopeRight (right foot must be $0C, same three conditions for the slope flag), followed by the slopeFracAccum step reduction. slopeFracAccum ($09C6): clamp negative to zero, += $24, step = accumulator >> 4; if the step is nonzero $24 becomes the step and the accumulator drops by step << 4, otherwise $24 is left at the full value. Net effect: alternating full and tiny steps (OQ-I033-3). player_move_controller zeroes the accumulator when the NS speed is zero.
SouthSlopeRight: Slope type $03 under the left foot. The right foot (ProbeCurrentBR) must be $03 as well, else SouthBlockedWall. Slope flag path (playerFlags $1000 via playerStateByte bit $10, then ApplyMovementDeltas): feet on a row line (CheckSubTileAlignY carry clear), or the cell above is also $03, or the new row offset is >= 8. Otherwise (misaligned, different cell above, offset < 8) plain ApplyMovementDeltas without the flag.
SouthStairsTile: Vine reached while walking south. Column-aligned (carry clear): go straight in. Straddling (carry set): the cell to the RIGHT must also be type $08, otherwise blocked (an older comment said the cell below). Sets playerFlags $0800 (script / ability lock) through the high byte playerStateByte, switches the player to ClimbVineEntry (which sets actor flag $0200 and hides the use-item button), clears the wait counter and floors Y through SnapYSouthCollision (which also zeroes playerSpeedNs).
SouthWallHandler: Current TL $06 while moving north. Current BR $06 too: ClearMovementDeltas. Otherwise ProbeFutureTL + CheckSubTileAlignY. Y straddling and future TL $06: gap chain (loc_02D19E): the east cell and the cell below it must both be type 0, else ClearSpeedNS_1; both empty: ComputeYSnapOffset + FineAdjustXWest (X moves EAST). Y flush or another type: SnapXWestCollision (X east to the next column centre), re-probe; $06 -> slide, else zero $24 + SnapYSouthCollision + apply.
SouthWallNorthInteract: Left foot (current BL) on type $09. If the current top-right is $09 too the player is stopped (ClearMovementDeltas). Otherwise ProbeFutureBL: when the row is not on a tile line and FutureBL is $09, the cell right of it and the cell above that must both be empty (any other result clears playerSpeedNs through ClearSpeedNS_3), then the slide runs. In every other case SnapXWestCollision moves X to the next tile centre east, FutureBL is probed again: type 0, $01 or $09 slides, any other type floors Y (SnapYSouthCollision) and applies the move. The slide is ComputeSouthSnapOffset then FineAdjustXWest.
SouthWallNorthProbe: FutureBL is type $09. If the cell right of it is solid ($0E+) the Y floor path at loc_02D516 runs (SnapYSouthCollision then ApplyMovementDeltas), otherwise it joins the gap test in SouthWallNorthInteract (loc_02D4F0).
SouthWallNudge: Future TL $06 while moving north. $AB bit 1 (the west horizontal phase ran this tick) with X flush: $24 = 0 and the X move is applied. Otherwise MapCellRight from the future TL cell: $0E and above -> loc_02D1BC (zero $24, SnapYSouthCollision, apply); anything else -> the SouthWallHandler gap chain at loc_02D19E (which cancels on any nonzero type).
SouthWallSouthInteract: Right foot (current BR) on type $06; mirror of SouthWallNorthInteract. Current top-left $06 stops the player. Otherwise ProbeFutureBR: when the row is off a tile line and FutureBR is $06 the cell left of it and the one above must be empty (else ClearSpeedNS_4), then the slide runs. In every other case SnapXEastCollision (X floored to the tile centre, i.e. moved WEST) and FutureBR is re-probed: still $06 slides; otherwise $24 is zeroed, SnapYNorthCollision runs and the move is applied. The slide is ComputeSouthSnapOffset then FineAdjustXEast. Using the NORTH snap here adds one extra row ($40) after the floor; see OQ-I033-2.
spc_sound_engine: Raw SPC700 machine code binary — the complete Quintet sound engine uploaded to the SPC700's 64KB RAM at boot time. Contains the audio driver, DSP register management, envelope tables, frequency lookup tables, and the music/SFX playback interpreter. This is not 65C816 code — it is SPC700 (Sony SPC-700) bytecode executed on the SNES audio coprocessor.
SpcBlockTransfer:
Upload one music track's data to the SPC700: two sessions over the stream at [$46] (callers: LoadMusicFromTransitionState and scene_script's music load).

Session 1: SpcIplHandshake sends the stream's leading records (the song's data and tables, ARAM $1254 ...) up to the size-0 terminator and returns with Y past it. Y is backed up by 2 to the terminator's destination word, which becomes $2E: the ARAM address of the first sample chunk. Port command $FF is written to APUIO0 (the engine re-enters its resident loader), $30 is set to $CC (first kick) and the routine waits for the fresh $BBAA.

Session 2: the next stream byte is the chunk count ($28), followed by that many chunk-index bytes (Y of the first one is kept in $32). Per index byte: bit 7 set = empty slot (skip via SpcChunkDone); otherwise $4A/$4C is reset to the library start $C5:0000, $2E += the previous chunk's size ($2C), and the loop at SpcFindChunk reads each chunk's size word and skips chunks (adding their sizes, wrapping at $8000 into the next bank) until the index reaches 0. The chosen chunk's size goes to X and $2C, the data pointer to Y; the header (destination to ports 2/3, flag in port 1, kick on port 0) is sent by SpcSendHeader and the data loop at SpcSendChunkData sends the bytes with the same counter handshake as SpcIplHandshake. The counter ($30) persists across chunks.

After the last chunk SpcChunkDone clears $2C and sends a size-0 record (port 1 = 0, V clear), ends the session, clears APUIO1/APUIO2 and returns. NMI is switched off around each header/kick (DisableNmiKeepJoypad) and back on after the kick echo when worldReadyFlag = $0F.
SpcChunkDone: Per-chunk bookkeeping and end of session inside SpcBlockTransfer (the data loop above falls into it; empty chunk slots jump here). Decrements the remaining chunk count ($28). While chunks remain it loops back to SpcNextChunkIndex for the next index byte. When the count is exhausted it clears the previous-size accumulator ($2C/$2D) and falls into SpcSendHeader with the running counter, which sends the final size-0 record (port 1 = 0, V clear) that ends the session.
SpcFindChunk: Walks the C5 sample library: for each header word at [$4A], subtracts one from the wanted index in $2A until zero, skipping payload bytes and wrapping $4A at 32K page boundaries; when the target chunk is found, sets Y to the data offset and branches into SpcSendHeader with the handshake counter from $30.
SpcIplHandshake:
Low-level SPC700 upload protocol (boot ROM IPL or the engine's resident clone of it). Waits for $BBAA on APUIO0/1, then sends the records at [$46] from Y = 0 until a size-0 record; returns with Y just past that record.

Per record (SpcSendRecord): size word → X, destination word → ports 2/3, DisableNmiKeepJoypad (NMI off), port 1 = 1 if the size is non-zero else 0 (ROL of the CPX #1 carry), ADC #$7F sets V when it was 1, then the kick (the counter pushed earlier; $CC for the first record) on port 0 and a wait for the echo; if worldReadyFlag = $0F the NMI is turned back on. BVS then sends the data bytes: the first byte with counter 0, each following byte as one 16-bit write (counter low, data high) after the SPC has echoed the previous counter. After the last byte the final echo is awaited and the counter advances by 4 (ADC #$03 with the carry set; a result of 0 is stepped over) to become the next kick.

The size-0 record ends the session (port 1 = 0, V clear); the routine then clears APUIO2 and returns with RTS. It is the shared low-level routine of SpcLoadBuiltinEngine and SpcBlockTransfer.
SpcLoadBuiltinEngine: Boot-time entry point for uploading the built-in sound engine to the SPC700 (called by SystemInit). Sets the data pointer [$46] to the spc_sound_engine blob (16-bit offset and bank byte), then calls SpcIplHandshake, which sends the blob's single record (3,018 bytes to ARAM $0400) and the terminator whose entry address $0400 makes the IPL start the engine.
SpcMusicLoadCmd: Load SPC music data when the room group matches. Reads musicParentActor and room group from script, loads ROM pointer, compares musicRoomGroup to script group — mismatch exits. CheckSourceCacheHit on $0687 skips redundant loads. On load: WaitFrames(26), optional stop ($F2 + 32 frames if $0D72 set), handshake ($F0 poll, $FF), SpcBlockTransfer from $46/$48, sets $0D72=1, then writes play ($01) or stop ($00) to APUIO0 based on musicParentActor.
SpcNextChunkIndex: Start of the per-chunk loop inside SpcBlockTransfer: resets the sample-library pointer to bank C5 page 0, reads the next chunk index byte from the stream at Y in $32, and skips to SpcChunkDone when bit 7 marks an empty slot; otherwise accumulates the running SPC destination offset and enters SpcFindChunk.
SpcSendChunkData: Byte loop for one library chunk after SpcSendHeader: reads from [$4A],Y with bank byte $4C, waits for APUIO0 echo, writes data and an incrementing counter to APUIO0/1, wraps Y at $8000, and exits when X (byte count) reaches zero.
SpcSendHeader: Shared block header inside SpcBlockTransfer (also reached from SpcChunkDone when all chunks are done): pushes the continuation counter, writes chunk size to the port handshake, SPC RAM dest to APUIO2/3, more-data flag to APUIO1, disables NMI around the kick, waits for APUIO0 echo, optionally re-enables NMI when worldReadyFlag is $0F, then branches to SpcSendChunkData if more bytes remain or clears ports and returns.
SpcSendRecord: IPL record sender inside SpcIplHandshake: pushes the kick counter, reads size and destination words from [$46],Y, disables NMI, writes port 1/2/3, kicks port 0 and waits for echo, restores NMI when worldReadyFlag is $0F, loops to the byte sender when overflow indicates data, else clears APUIO2 and returns with the saved P.
SpinDashChargeTick: One tick of the Spin Dash charge. $26 is the charge level (it starts at $0F). When $26 is odd the L button ($0020) must be newly pressed to decrement it, when even the R button ($0010). The routine then adds the L/R bits that are pressed to joypadHeld, which consumes them: joypadCurrent no longer reports a held shoulder button, so every decrement needs a fresh press. Starting at $0F the sequence L, R, L, R reaches $0B; once $26 is below $0C SpinDashMain leaves the charge phase and spawns the guided projectile.
StartForcedWalk:
Spawn a direction-specific forced walk actor on the player.

Sets playerFlags $0100 (forced walk active) and player actor flag $2000 (COP-script mode). Clears scrollStepIndex. Decodes the walk direction from scrollStepTableBase:
  Bit 5 ($0020): West → ForcedWalkWest
  Bit 4 ($0010): East → ForcedWalkEast
  Bit 7 ($0080): North → ForcedWalkNorth
  Default: South → ForcedWalkSouth

Keeps only the low nibble of scrollStepTableBase ($000F), the walk sequence index the ForcedWalk actors use. Each direction variant uses PHD to set the player actor as DP, spawns via COP [SpawnBefore], then restores DP.
StatusAbilityRow0: Ability row 3 actor (topmost, Y=$0048). Sprite = characterForm × 3 + $44.
StatusAbilityRow1: Ability row 2 actor (middle, Y=$0060). Sprite = characterForm × 3 + $45.
StatusAbilityRow2: Ability row 1 actor (bottom, Y=$0078). Sprite = characterForm × 3 + $46.
StatusConfirmExit: Exit the Status tab. SFX #11, consumes the confirm and cancel bits ($C000), kills the cursor, returns to InventoryMainLoop.
StatusCursorDown: Move status cursor down. INC $22; wraps 3 → 0 via CMP #3 guard.
StatusCursorPositions: Screen positions for 3 status rows: ($0098,$0048), ($0098,$0060), ($0098,$0078). Fixed X, Y increments by $18.
StatusCursorUp: Move status cursor up. DEC $22; wraps 0 → 2 via BPL guard.
StatusPositionCursor: Position status cursor from StatusCursorPositions. $22 × 4 indexes the table; writes X/Y to cursor actor $0014/$0016,Y.
StatusViewTab: Status tab handler. Sets bg1ConfigMode = 0, draws the status strings, spawns a cursor, $22 = 0. For the row in $22 it tests the ability flag of the current form (TestAbilityFlag with $0004 = characterForm) and, if unlocked, prints its description (ComputeAbilityIndex + RunBg3Script). Polls Up/Down for the row cursor and $C000 (A or B) → StatusConfirmExit.
StoreMapAndDecompress: Store map parameters and decompress one layer's tilemap. X selects layer (0 = primary, 2 = secondary): stores row stride ($01) and column count ($03) to mapRowStrideL0+X / $0697+X, computes total byte count via Multiply8x8Unsigned → $069B+X, then decompresses map data via QuintetLZ directly to mapTilemapBaseA+X. HandleEmptyGeometry is the alternate entry for zero-size compressed maps.
SystemInitConstants: 34 entries of [destination word, value word] terminated by a destination word with bit 15 set (a lone FFFF in the ROM). See the block note for the meaning of each group.
TabActionDispatch: Jump table for tab action handlers. 4 entries: UseItemTab (0), ArrangeItemsTab (1), DiscardItemTab (2), StatusViewTab (3).
TabCancel: Set exit flag byte #00 (polled by the main loop of inventory_overlay, which then tears the menu down) and return carry clear. The cancel bits are not consumed, so InventoryMainLoop keeps passing through here each frame until the overlay ends.
TabClearCursor: Clear the four tab cursor cells ($7F0784 / $0804 / $0884 / $0904) with the blank tile (tile $2060 in this baserom). Sets displayModeFlags bit 0.
TabConfirm: Tab confirm. Consumes A, draws cursor, carry set.
TabConfirmDispatch: Play confirm SFX (#$0D), store current tab to $18 and $0000, dispatch through TabActionDispatch via SwitchCase.
TabDrawCursor: Draw tab cursor on BG3. Offset = inventoryTabIndex × $0100 >> 1 + $0584. Tile $202B at $7F0200+offset.
TabHoverArrange: Arrange tab hover preview. Shows the item slots and the equip cursor and draws the Arrange description. It does not hide the status actors: the neighbours of tab 1 are the Use and Discard previews, which already did.
TabHoverDiscard: Discard tab hover preview. Shows the item slots and the equip cursor, hides the equipped-item display and status rows, draws the Discard strings and sets bg1ConfigMode = 4.
TabHoverDispatch: Jump table for tab hover preview handlers. 4 entries: TabHoverUse (0), TabHoverArrange (1), TabHoverDiscard (2), TabHoverStatus (3).
TabHoverStatus: Status tab hover preview. HIDES the 16 item slots and the equip cursor, draws the status strings (character info), shows the equipped-item display if something is equipped, then walks the three status row actors (chain head moveYAlt = StatusAbilityRow0, the top row, then the $0006 links). For row r = 0..2 it tests flag characterForm×4 + r (TestAbilityFlag); if set it unhides the row actor and prints the ability name (ComputeAbilityIndex + RunBg3Script). The rows are ability slots 0–2 of the current form, not Will/Freedan/Shadow.
TabHoverUse: Use tab hover preview. Shows the 16 item slots (ShowAllItemSlots), shows the equip cursor if something is equipped, hides the equipped-item display and the status rows (HideStatusActors), draws the Use tab strings and sets bg1ConfigMode = 4.
TabSelectionLoop: Tab bar poll, once per frame. A ($8000) → TabConfirm, Up/Down → TabSelectUp/Down, mask $6000 (B or Select) → TabCancel. Blink counter $1C draws or clears the cursor every 16 frames. Carry set = confirmed.
TabSelectUp: Tab up. DEC inventoryTabIndex, AND $0003. Redraws cursor.
TestAbilityFlag: Test ability unlock: flag index = $0004 (characterForm) × 4 + A (slot). Calls TestFlag_0510. Carry set = unlocked.
TileCoordsToMapIndex: DP $18 = tile X, $1C = tile Y, X register = layer selector (0 = layer 0, 2 = layer 1; picks mapRowStrideL0 or L1). Returns X = map index (see the block note for the format). Preserves P through PHP/PLP; 16 callers.
TileProbeMain:
Core tile collision probe: converts pixel coordinates to a collision type.

Entry: $1A = X pixel, $1E = Y pixel. Both must lie inside the camera bounds (cameraOffsetX <= $1A < cameraBoundsX, cameraOffsetY <= $1E < cameraLowerYBound; negative values are rejected). Out of bounds: $00 = X = $4001, A = $0F, carry set.

In bounds: tile column $18 = $1A >> 4 and tile row $1C = $1E >> 4, CalcTileMapOffset (tile_collision_physics) returns the map index in Y, stored in $00 and passed in X to ReadCollisionNibble. Returns A = collision type with carry SET when it is nonzero (any slope, ladder, wall type or solid tile, not only blocking ones; solid is A >= $0E) and carry clear when it is zero.
TrailPositionCascade:
3-stage position FIFO cascade for the Dark Friar fragment trail followers.

Each call reads the oldest stage as the follower's displayed $14/$16, shifts the other two stages forward and samples the position of the actor in Y (the caller loads $04, the previous actor-list entry) into the newest stage. The follower therefore trails that actor by 3 calls. The X queue is animScratch, animScratch+2, animScratch2; the Y queue is moveXAlt, moveYAlt, retPtr1.
TrailPositionInit:
Initialize trail follower position FIFO.

Sets all three FIFO stages to the follower's own current position ($14 / $16, its spawn position), so the delayed trail starts co-located instead of at (0,0). Called once by the shared trail follower entry (loc_02BDFE) of TrailFollowerSprA and TrailFollowerSprB.
UnfreezeCameraAfterAttack: Called when Psycho Dash animation completes: clears layerPriorityFlag $0200 so the camera scrolls again, then falls through into RunAttackCleanup.
UnsignedDivide:
16÷8 unsigned hardware divide.

Input: Y = 16-bit dividend (WRDIVL/WRDIVH), A = 8-bit divisor (WRDIVB, which starts the divide).
Output: A low = quotient low byte (RDDIVL), A high = remainder (RDMPYL), assembled with XBA. The quotient's high byte is not returned.
8 NOPs (16 cycles) cover the divide latency.
UpdateScrollColumn:
Determines which vertical column to render when horizontal scrolling crosses a tile boundary.

Computes the X position of the newly-visible column based on scroll direction: if scrolling left (negative delta), uses offset 0 (left screen edge); if scrolling right (positive delta), uses +256 ($0100, the screen width) for the right edge.

Sets $18 = computed X position, $1C = current vertical scroll, then calls RenderColumnStrip to render that column of tiles into the staging buffer.
UpdateScrollRow:
Determines which horizontal row to render when vertical scrolling crosses a tile boundary.

Sets $18 to the current horizontal scroll (full X extent for the row). Computes the Y position of the newly-visible row based on scroll direction: if scrolling up (negative delta), uses −16 to get the top screen edge; if scrolling down (positive delta), uses +224 ($00E0) to get the bottom edge (14 tiles × 16px).

The Y position is added to the current vertical scroll and then wrapped against mapBoundsY via a subtraction loop to handle maps that wrap vertically.

Finally calls RenderRowStrip to render that row of tiles into the staging buffer for V-Blank DMA.
UpdateSlotActorSprite: Walk the slot actor chain (orbitAngle, $0006 links) to the Nth actor (A = slot index) and reset it: entry point ($0000) = SlotActorEvaluate, $28/$08/$2A = 0 so it re-evaluates empty/non-empty. Returns with Y = that slot ACTOR (not the slot index); callers use it for STA $0028,Y.
UploadCgramPalette: VBlank DMA (called by NmiHandler every frame, by the camera refresh and by the inventory overlay): CGADD = 0, then 512 bytes from WRAM $7F:0A00 through DMA channel 0 to CGRAM ($2122). Afterwards the three bytes at $7F:0C00-$7F:0C02 are written verbatim to COLDATA ($2132); each byte must therefore carry its own channel-select bits (blue $80, green $40, red $20) and a 5-bit intensity. Entry contract: A 8-bit, X 16-bit (no REP/SEP for X).
UploadOamTable: VBlank DMA (called by NmiHandler every frame): OAMADD = 0, then $0220 bytes (512 main table + 32 high-table bytes) from WRAM $0422 through DMA channel 0 to the OAM port ($2104). Entry contract: X 16-bit, A 8-bit as left by the NMI.
UseItemConfirm: Confirm item selection in the Use tab. Consumes the confirm and cancel bits ($C000), stores $1A → inventoryEquippedIndex. Empty slot (item byte 0): inventoryEquippedIndex = $1A = $FFFF and inventoryEquippedType = 0. Otherwise stores the item ID in inventoryEquippedType. Both paths return to InventoryMainLoop.
UseItemCursorDown: Move the equip cursor down one row in the Use tab. Consumes Down, Left and Right ($0700), SFX #10, $1A + 4 with AND $000F wrapping.
UseItemCursorLeft: Move equip cursor left one column in Use tab. $1A − 1 with AND $000F wrapping.
UseItemCursorRight: Move equip cursor right one column in Use tab. $1A + 1 with AND $000F wrapping. Uses JMP instead of BRA (out of branch range).
UseItemCursorUp: Move the equip cursor up one row in the Use tab. Consumes Up, Left and Right ($0B00), SFX #10, $1A − 4 with AND $000F wrapping, then back to UseItemRefreshCursor.
UseItemRefreshCursor: Use-tab loop head: positions the equip cursor from $1A, runs BG3 item list and detail scripts, yields, and branches on D-pad or confirm masks; entered from UseItemTab and after cursor moves.
UseItemTab: Use tab action handler. Sets bg1ConfigMode = 4, draws the item grid strings, writes inventoryEquippedIndex = 0 (a non-negative placeholder so ShowEquipCursor reveals the cursor; UseItemConfirm always overwrites it), clamps $1A to 0 if negative, positions the equip cursor, prints the item name for the cursor slot via itemAbilityIndex, then polls every frame: A or B (mask $C000) → UseItemConfirm, D-pad → cursor moves. There is no cancel in this tab.
VBlankPartial: Partial VBlank handler — skips the NMI wait and performs the Mode 7 upload and joypad processing only. Its only caller is UpdateFrameFull (system_core), which the NMI handler runs while a music upload is in progress; the NMI has already stored a fresh joypadRaw by then. Saves P and the 16-bit accumulator (PHA under REP #$20), switches to 8-bit A and branches into the section shared with VBlankWaitAndJoypad.
VBlankWaitAndJoypad:
Full VBlank synchronization with Mode 7 register upload and joypad input processing.

Polls RDNMI ($4210) until bit 7 is set (VBlank started), then falls through to the Mode 7 upload and the complete joypad pipeline: inject check, button remapping, consumption mask update, auto-repeat, and edge detection.

RDNMI is read before the loop (clears a stale flag), in the loop, and once more after it; reading the register clears the flag, so the extra read after the loop changes nothing. The caller normally has NMI enabled while it waits, so the NMI handler runs inside the poll loop and refreshes joypadRaw before the remap below. Saves and restores A and P only (see the block note for the X clobber in Mode 7).

See the vblank_joypad block note for detailed descriptions of each pipeline stage.
WaitFrames:
Wait for A frames by calling VBlankWaitAndJoypad in a loop.

Entry: A = number of frames to wait (A = 0 would wait 256 frames with an 8-bit A, 65,536 with a 16-bit A). VBlankWaitAndJoypad preserves A, so the DEC counts the frames. Joypad state is updated every frame during the wait only if the NMI runs (see the block note).
WallSlidePushDown:
Y push of the north-side wall slide (code_02DC4B / code_02DC77 chain); also used by player_move_east. Mirror of WallSlidePushUp.

Uses the complemented Y sub-tile nibble; the valid push is POSITIVE ($02 << 2 in $24, Y grows, down) and the overshoot case clears $AA bits $0440. The original player_move_east comments called this push 'slide upward'; the arithmetic says downward and the east notes now agree (UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME, OQ-I029-4).
WallSlidePushUp:
Y push of the south-side wall slide (code_02DC9F / code_02DCCB chain); also used by player_move_east.

Adds the Y sub-tile position (($26 >> 2) & $0F, or $10 when zero) to the offset in $02. A total below $11 applies the movement unchanged. Otherwise $02 = total & $0F and the horizontal speed is compared with the vertical velocity parked on PlayerMovementTick's stack ($03,S): no vertical velocity or horizontal larger stores a NEGATIVE push (-$02 << 2) in $24, which ApplyMovementDeltas adds to Y (up); equal magnitudes cancel both velocities; smaller drops $20 and clears $AA bits $0840.
WestRampAscend:
Handler for an east-facing slope ($0A) while walking west. Mirror of WestRampDescend.

Four probes look for a $0A tile: the current BL probe moved to X + 8, the cell above it (MapCellUp), the future TL at X + 8, and the cell below that (MapCellDown). None found goes to DiagRedirectToNorth. The Y step is the negation of the west ramp's: Y -= (16 - sub-tile) << 2 and one pixel less when bit 2 of the sum is set; the full-tile entry code_02DEE4 adds $20 (negative) to $26. Y shrinks, so the player climbs to the left. Post-ramp wall check as in WestRampDescend (code_02DF4C / code_02DF54).
WestRampDescend:
Handler for a west-facing slope ($05) while walking west.

Four probes look for a $05 tile: the current TL probe moved to X + 8 (the centre column), the cell below it (MapCellDown), the future TL at X + 8, and the cell below that. None found goes to DiagRedirectToSouth. Found: if the move does not cross a 16-pixel column (CheckTileBoundaryXor) the movement is applied unchanged; otherwise Y += (16 - sub-tile) << 2 with sub-tile = (($22 + $20) >> 2) & $0F, plus one more pixel when bit 2 of ($26 + $20 + $22) is set. The full-tile entry code_02DD82 adds the negated X velocity to $26 instead. Y grows, so the player descends to the left.

Then sets playerFlags $1000 and runs the post-ramp wall check: future TL and BL both below $0E apply the movement, only BL blocked goes to code_02DDF2 (SnapYSouthCollision), only TL blocked goes to code_02DDFA (SnapYNorthCollision), both blocked snaps X to a tile centre and compensates Y.
WestRampDown: Entered from DispatchEastMove when ProbeCurrentBL read $05. Samples (X, bottom + 1) for $05; no crossing -> code_02DA0E (Y -= $20); crossing: $24 = 4n - $20 (n as in EastRampUp), negative (upward) while 4n < $20. Y grows downward, so the older 'positive, producing upward displacement' was wrong. Finishes at code_02DA19.
WestRampEdgeAscend:
Slope-edge handler reached from ProbeCurrentTR finding a $0A tile. Mirror of WestRampEdgeDescend.

Probes at the TR point moved 9 pixels left in X; if that tile is $0A, a column crossing computes the edge offset into $24 (Y adjustment) and continues at code_02DEEB, otherwise the full-tile ramp (code_02DEE4) runs.
WestRampEdgeDescend:
Slope-edge handler reached from ProbeCurrentTR finding a $05 tile at the trailing corner.

Probes at the TR point moved 9 pixels left in X (net X - 1, top row). If that tile is $05: no column crossing means the full-tile ramp (code_02DD82); otherwise an edge offset is computed from the X velocity and stored in $24 (a Y adjustment), then execution continues at code_02DD8D (set playerFlags $1000 and the post-ramp wall check). Not a slope: the movement is applied unchanged.
WestRampUp: Entered when FindSlopeForEastMove found $05. Mirror of EastRampDown: BR probe at (X, bottom + 1), MapCellUp on the first retry, FutureTR at (X + step - 1) then MapCellDown, and negated Y (crossing: $26 -= 4n with a -4 bias; direct: $26 -= $20). Finishes at code_02DA19 with the same snaps.
WestRedirectToSouth:
Fallback when no $05 slope is found after the WestRampDown probe sequence.

Probes FutureBR: if $06 (south wall) → redirect to EastWallSouthDiag. Otherwise → ApplyMovementDeltas.
WillAttackPaletteFX: Will charge-up tint. Bundle #2A is 14 one-frame strips of 15 colors at CGRAM $81–$8F (sprite palette 0, colors 1–15) with holds 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0, i.e. 62 ticks per pass; PaletteStartLoop/PaletteStepLoop play it twice. Bundle #2B holds the same 14 color sets with no holds (14 ticks per pass) and is repeated until AttackCleanup kills the actor.
WrapMapIndex:
Wraps a map data index back within valid tilemap bounds.

Subtracts the tilemap base address ($069E+X) and the map data size ($069A+X; inferred from the arithmetic — it is the wrap modulus) from the current index. If no borrow occurs (carry set), the index has overflowed past the end of the map data — the base is re-added, leaving index − size, and the check repeats until the index normalizes.

Stores the wrapped index to DP $04 and Y register. Called by both RenderRowStrip and RenderColumnStrip whenever map access indices might exceed the allocated tilemap region.
WriteMapBounds: Write map dimension bounds for one BG layer and transfer map data. Stores X bounds ($00) to mapBoundsX+X and Y bounds ($02) to mapBoundsY+X, then calls DmaRomToWram using current $0664/$0666/$0668 and destination in $42/$44. X selects layer (0 or 2).
YesNoClearCursor: Clear the two Yes/No cursor cells ($7F0896 = No row, $7F0916 = Yes row) with the blank tile (tile $2060 in this baserom). Sets displayModeFlags bit 0 to flag the BG3 tilemap as dirty.
YesNoConfirm: Confirm Yes/No. Consumes A, draws cursor, returns carry set.
YesNoDrawCursor: Draw Yes/No cursor on BG3. Offset = $28 × $0100 >> 1 + $0696. Tile $202B at $7F0200+offset.
YesNoPromptLoop: Yes/No prompt poll, once per frame. A ($8000) → YesNoConfirm (B does not cancel); Up/Down toggle $28 (0 = No on the first row, 1 = Yes). Blink counter $1C: every 16 frames the cursor is drawn (bit 4 clear) or cleared (bit 4 set). Carry set = answered.
YesNoSelectUp: Toggle Yes/No up. DEC $28, AND $0001. Redraws cursor.
